commits.pr_title: [ROCm][CI] Bump the ROCm 10 image to torch 2.13
commits.pr_body:
- Bump `TORCH_VERSION` to `2.13.0+rocm10.0.0` and `TORCHVISION_VERSION` to `0.28.0+rocm10.0.0` in `Dockerfile.rocm_base`
- Release the piecewise CUDA graphs on ROCm in Model Runner V2's `shutdown()` before distributed teardown, as the V1 runner already does

When #58761 made the TheRock image the default, AMD CI went from torch 2.13 (the ROCm 7.2 image, bumped in #50605) back to 2.12, because the TheRock Dockerfile never got that bump. #61118 sets `torch._inductor.config.batch_invariant`, which only exists from torch 2.13, so every engine started with `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` died with `AttributeError: torch._inductor.config.batch_invariant does not exist` (Batch Invariance on MI250/MI300/MI355, the DPX LoRA shards, LoRA TP and Spec Decode Draft Model since https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/95651). #62274 now skips the setting when torch lacks it; this restores the inductor batch-invariant mode on ROCm. This goes to 2.13 rather than 2.14, which is what the ROCm 7.2 image runs: 2.14's ATen headers require C++20, while the pinned flash-attention builds its ROCm extension with `-std=c++17`, so the base image fails to build with 2.14 (https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/95690). This supersedes #59658, which made the same bump against `Dockerfile.rock_base` before #58761 renamed it.

`:amd: (MI355) Distributed DP + EP` still aborts at exit with `terminate called without an active exception` after #62241 (https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/95767). The MoE all-gather on the DP group is captured in the piecewise graphs, and RCCL's `ncclCommAbort` waits until every graph that captured the communicator is destroyed (ROCm/rocm-systems#13018). The V2 runner never released them, so the abort hung on every rank with a cold compile cache, `PyNcclCommunicator.destroy()` gave up after its 5 s join, and the process exited with the abort still inside RCCL (stack: `ncclCommAbort_impl -> commReclaim -> commDestroySync -> condition_variable::wait`). On 8x MI355 with the CI command and a fresh cache each run, the abort now finishes in under 1 s in 10/10 runs with every PyNccl communicator destroyed, and the `Distributed Torchrun + Shutdown` commands and the V2 runner tests pass. As in V1, `clear_all_graphs()` is process-wide.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to draft this change. Every line was reviewed by the submitter.

commits.pr_title: [Frontend] systemone: prefill the shared prefix once before the reads on hybrid models
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`/v1/systemone` on hybrid (Mamba/linear-attention) models prefilled the state once per question, because reads that start together cannot reuse each other's recurrent state. This sends one request for the tokens all questions share before the reads, so each question only prefills its own text. Related: #59299 (endpoint), #60677.

## Claims

- Hybrid model, prefix caching on, 2+ questions: 4 questions 25.3 → 8.1 s, 16 questions 106.5 → 12.0 s, 64 questions 419 → 28.7 s (p50, 2k-token state). Prefix-cache hit rate 0.37 → 0.94.
- Throughput with 8 questions of a 1k-token state per request: 0.027 → 0.17 req/s.
- A single question is unchanged (6.4 s). Answers are unchanged (label accuracy on 120 synthetic tickets identical: 0.90 / 0.67 / 1.00).
- No change on attention-only models or with prefix caching off: the warm-up is skipped.

## Validation

Qwen3.8-27B (Qwen3_5 hybrid, 4-bit, MTP 3) on gfx1151 (Radeon 8060S), nightly `0.31.1rc1.dev273` (`2eb491e18b`), `--enable-prefix-caching --mamba-cache-mode align --prefix-match-unit 32 --logprobs-mode raw_logprobs`. Same seed and prompts in both columns, p50 latency of a `/v1/systemone` call, state of 2048 tokens:

| questions | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 6.4 s | 6.4 s |
| 4 | 25.3 s | 8.1 s |
| 16 | 106.5 s | 12.0 s |
| 64 | 419.1 s | 28.7 s |

| config | 4 q | 16 q | 64 q |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--enable-mamba-shared-prefix-checkpoint`, main → PR | 14.1 → 8.1 s | 36.4 → 11.9 s | 126.3 → 28.7 s |
| MTP off, `--prefix-match-unit 16`, main → PR | 11.6 → 7.2 s | 42.8 → 10.0 s | n/a → 21.2 s |

The warm-up alone gives the full gain; the checkpoint flag is not needed with it (8.1 / 12.0 / 28.7 s with and without).

Attention-only model (Qwen3-0.6B, prefix caching on), warm-up forced on for the test: 4 questions 0.375 → 0.399 s, 16 questions 0.538 → 0.564 s, since the blocks are already shared within a step there. That is why the warm-up is limited to hybrid models.

Tests:

```bash
pytest tests/entrypoints/generate/structured_decisions/test_strategies.py
```

28 passed on main `56e3b08` (`test_common_prefix_len` and `test_state_is_prefilled_once_before_the_reads` are this PR's). The new test checks the order and content of the engine calls (warm-up request first, with `cache_salt`, then the reads, all starting with the same ids) and the four cases where it is skipped (attention-only, prefix caching off, one question, short state).

Reproduction: a client posting `/v1/systemone` with a fresh synthetic state of 2048 tokens and N filler `choice` questions, after one 2-question warm-up call; p50 over 3 repetitions per N, same seed for both columns; server flags as above.

## Details

- The warm-up is a `max_tokens=1` request on the longest common token prefix of the question prompts (at least 128 tokens), sent with the request's `cache_salt`, priority, LoRA and trace headers. Its prompt-end checkpoint lands where the questions diverge, so each read resumes there and only prefills its question.
- Cost: one extra scheduler round trip when the state is cold. Skipped for one question, a prefix under 128 tokens, prefix caching off, or a non-hybrid model.
- Not covered: Mamba state kept by connectors, and models other than the one above. The change is in `NextTokenStrategy`, so the diffusion strategy inherits it; it was not run.
- Overlaps with the open #61251 (tokenizes the state once per decision and adds a gate for big decisions), which edits the same `read`: if that lands first, the warm-up request should go through its gate; I will rebase on whichever lands first.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Qwen4Exp] Remove the Qwen3.8-Flash-Next TEP8 MXFP4 emulation guard
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Removes `_requires_qwen38_tep8_emulation`, which forces OCP MX emulation for Qwen3.8 Flash Next's (`amd/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Quark-MXFP4`) routed experts at TEP8 on gfx950 when the fused shared expert is off. The guard was added because AITER padded the MoE width from 640 to 768 for that shape and the native W4A4 kernel lost accuracy. Since #55104 aligns the W4A4 intermediate to 128, Flash Next's width stays at 640 with no pad, and the native kernel is as accurate as emulation and about twice as fast.

Existing work:
* #55104 removed the pad that the guard worked around, and on its own fixes Flash Next's accuracy at EP4 and TEP8 (measured below) and at TP1 (0.9651, #55104 on `nightly-43b4aaea`).
* The first revision of this PR also changed the pad rounding at MoE `tp_size == 1`. With #55104 merged, that is a no-op for Flash Next, so it is dropped here.

## Claims

- At TEP8 with `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=0`, the only configuration where the guard fires, the native AITER W4A4 kernel matches emulation's accuracy (GSM8K 0.9651 vs 0.9629) at 2.3x the output throughput at 8k/1k concurrency 4 (362 vs 158 tok/s) and 1.9x at concurrency 32 (1399 vs 741).
- No change for the checkpoint card's recipe: with the fused shared expert each rank holds 65 local experts, the guard requires exactly 64, so it never fired there.
- No change for any other shape: the guard matched only `E=512, H=2560, N=640` at EP8 on gfx950.

## Validation

**Unit tests** (MI355X, gfx950, `nightly-5555a2d8` with this PR): 5 passed.

```bash
pytest -v -s tests/quantization/test_gfx950_moe.py
```

`test_qwen38_tep8_selects_native_aiter` replaces the guard's two tests: the TEP8 shape now selects `AITER_MXFP4_MXFP4` under both `auto` and `aiter`.

**Accuracy**, GSM8K 5-shot, all 1319 questions, MI355X, the checkpoint card's recipe, `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-5555a2d8` vs the same image with this PR, one run per cell. Exact match, higher is better:

| config | stock | this PR |
| ------ | ----- | ------- |
| TEP8, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=0` | 0.9629 (emulation, guard hit) | 0.9651 (native) |
| TEP8, the card's recipe | 0.9644 (native, guard not hit) | unchanged |
| EP4 (TP4 + `--enable-expert-parallel`) | 0.9636 (native) | unchanged |

Flexible-extract; strict-match for the first row is 0.9636 → 0.9659. Standard error is about 0.005.

**Throughput**, TEP8 with `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=0`, emulation (stock) vs native (this PR), random dataset, one run per cell. Output tok/s is higher-is-better, mean TPOT lower-is-better:

| ISL / OSL | Conc | Output tok/s, emulation → native | Mean TPOT (ms), emulation → native |
| --------- | ---- | -------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- |
| 8192 / 1024 | 4 | 158 → 362 | 24.2 → 9.5 |
| 8192 / 1024 | 32 | 741 → 1399 | 38.7 → 20.0 |
| 128 / 8 | 1 | 40 → 90 | 21.2 → 7.2 |

**Reproduce:**

```bash
# plus the checkpoint card's ROCm environment, identical in both arms
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=0 \
vllm serve amd/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Quark-MXFP4 --tensor-parallel-size 8 --enable-expert-parallel \
  --max-model-len 262144 --no-enable-prefix-caching --trust-remote-code \
  --default-chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking": false}'
lm_eval --model local-completions --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --apply_chat_template \
  --model_args model=amd/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Quark-MXFP4,base_url=http://localhost:8000/v1/completions,max_gen_toks=2048,num_concurrent=32
```

## Details

* **Why the guard is stale.** Its docstring says AITER pads `N` to 768 for this shape. Since #55104 the W4A4 intermediate is aligned to 128, so 640 is stored as is, with no pad. The native kernel at 640 is accurate (first accuracy row), so CK-Tile's `inter_dim % 256` scale issue does not show up for this shape.
* **When the guard fired.** It matches `num_local_experts == 64`. The fused shared expert adds one local expert per rank (`ExpertMapManager`), so with the card's recipe the count is 65 and the native kernel already ran; only `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=0` hit the guard.
* Only the ROCm MXFP4 oracle changes; nothing changes on CUDA.

**Limitations and CI gaps.**

* gfx950 only. The W4A4 MXFP4 MoE path does not run on gfx942.
* The end-to-end image applied the previous revision of this PR, which also changed the pad rounding at MoE `tp_size == 1`. With #55104, Flash Next's pad there is 0, so that part did nothing in these runs; the guard removal is the same code.
* The unit tests run in the AMD kernels CI job. The accuracy and throughput runs happened outside CI.

```bash
  --random-input-len 131072 --random-output-len 1024 --ignore-eos --temperature 0 \
  --num-prompts $N --max-concurrency $C --seed 43

  --model_args model=amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/completions,num_concurrent=64,tokenized_requests=False

VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 pytest -v tests/kernels/test_top_k_per_row.py \

```

## Details

- Gate: compress ratio 1 and k=2048 only. Decode always takes AITER (FULL graphs are not keyed by context length); prefill when `chunk.max_seqlen_k`, a host int, reaches 32K.
- Cost: with max_model_len between 131072 and 200000 and up to 48 rows, AITER loses 3-6 us per layer below 8-16K context. DeepSeek-V3.2 (default 163840, 61 indexer layers) measures +0.085 ms TPOT at 4K/1K c1. Keeping the in-tree kernel for that width band would also give up the 2.53 ms gain at 128K on the same deployment, so the gate does not exclude it.
- Not measured end to end: GLM-5/5.1, TP8. CI (MI300, NVIDIA) runs only the new selection test; the GPU tests need gfx950.

<details>
<summary>Design notes, pre-existing failure and related PRs</summary>

- Cause: the in-tree decode kernel has gfx950 policies only for k=512 and k=1024 (#55327). At k=2048 its cost grows with context; AITER's stays near flat.
- Semantics come from #52882's wrappers. ROCm DSA decode carries `(B, next_n)` bounds for native MTP1 and one row per token otherwise, so `seq_lens.reshape(-1)` with `next_n=1` gives AITER each row's exact end. Prefill turns AITER's chunk-global indices into sequence-local ones and keeps `-1`.
- Decode is not split by context length because a FULL graph replays one kernel for every length. Eager decode could use the length, but would then pick a different kernel for the same shape depending on graph mode. AITER's extra host time per call only shows in eager steps.
- `test_aiter_decode_topk_matches_per_row_under_mtp` (from #58167, `requires_gfx950`, so not in CI) fails identically on main: it passes `(B, 1)` seq_lens with `next_n=4` to the in-tree k=512 gfx950 kernel, which reads any 2-D `seq_lens` per row, so its reference rows are wrong. It does not reach the code changed here.
- #60012 (open) tunes the in-tree k=2048 kernel above 200000 columns for #55327. With this PR it still serves AITER-off deployments and short prefill chunks; the gate should be re-measured if it lands. #57844 (open) edits the same selector. #59421 (draft, native MTP above `next_n=2`) is compatible because decode flattens the bounds.
- #50470 (draft) and #46172 also move the k=2048 decode top-k to AITER. Both have merge conflicts and no activity since 2026-08-22, and both swap the call unconditionally, passing vLLM's `next_n` with its 2-D MTP bounds. On both, the author of #52882 noted that AITER v0.1.19 needs those bounds adapted and asked to treat #52882 as the consolidated direction; #52882 then merged with AITER enabled for compressed indexers only. This PR applies its adapters to the k=2048 path, adds prefill and serving results, and leaves every other indexer unchanged. The `aiter.top_k_per_row_decode` entry point that #50470 waited for ships in AITER 0.1.25 and is the function called here.
- Duplicate search, `gh pr list --state all --search`: "aiter topk", "top-k ROCm", "topk ROCm", "indexer ROCm", "indexer aiter", "DeepSeek-V3.2 ROCm", "GLM-5 ROCm", "sparse indexer AMD", "top_k_per_row_decode", "top_k_per_row_prefill", "compress_ratio aiter topk".

</details>

Not a duplicate: #50470 and #46172 target the same decode call, have been inactive since 2026-08-22, and were marked superseded by #52882's author; #52882 left k=2048 on the in-tree kernel (details above). Thanks @JH-Leon-KIM-AMD for #50470.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Scheduler] Fix encoder cache deadlock with drafter look-ahead
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Fixes the encoder-cache deadlock with a drafter look-ahead (EAGLE / MTP) reported in the second half of #40707 ([comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/40707#issuecomment-5760731067)). When two multimodal items only fit in the encoder cache one at a time and the gap between them is smaller than `2 * num_prefill_lookahead`, the request hangs forever, getting 0 scheduled tokens on every step with no error or log. The Mamba-alignment half of #40707 was already fixed by #51603.

## Claims

- A request with adjacent multimodal items that can't share the encoder cache now finishes under speculative decoding instead of hanging. Before this change it hung whenever `gap < 2 * L`, where `L = num_prefill_lookahead`.
- Output doesn't change. With temperature 0 the text matches the no-spec baseline exactly, and no `Encoder cache miss` was observed.

## Validation

**E2E** (1x GB200, MRV2, async scheduling on, prefix caching off): `Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B`, MTP with `num_speculative_tokens=1` (L=1). Each request has two 3008x4032 images of 11844 tokens each; the encoder cache is 16384, so only one image fits at a time. I used raw prompts to control how many tokens sit between the two `<|image_pad|>` runs, and confirmed the placeholder offsets in the scheduler (gap=0 gives `[(4, 11844), (11848, 11844)]`).

| | gap=0 | gap=1 | gap=2 |
|---|---|---|---|
| main, MTP | **hang** (no completion in 300 s) | **hang** | OK |
| this PR, MTP | OK (2 runs) | OK | OK |
| main, no spec (baseline) | OK | OK | OK |

At temperature 0, every OK run with this PR produces the same text as the no-spec baseline for the same prompt: "The first image contains a red circle, and the second image contains a blue rectangle." MTP acceptance was 9/9 drafts in all spec runs.

<details>
<summary>Scheduler-level sweep (L x gap; image=600 tokens, cache=900)</summary>

| L \ gap | 0 | 1 | 2 | 4 | 8 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 (main) | ok | ok | ok | ok | ok |
| 1 (main) | hang | hang | ok | ok | ok |
| 3 (main) | hang | hang | hang | hang | ok |
| 1, 3 (this PR) | ok | ok | ok | ok | ok |

#59030 at `17d95d3eb8` gives the same results as main in this sweep.
</details>

## Details

**Root cause.** Two places offset by the drafter look-ahead `L`, in opposite directions:

1. `_free_encoder_inputs` keeps item 1 until `num_computed_tokens >= end1 + L`. This was added in #46315.
2. When item 2 can't be allocated, `_try_schedule_encoder_inputs` stops the chunk at `start2 - L`.

If `start2 - L < end1 + L`, then `num_computed_tokens` can never reach the point where item 1 is freed, so item 2 is never allocated.

**Fix.** Remove the `L` offset in both places:

- **Free** once `end <= num_computed_tokens - num_output_placeholders`, as without spec decode. Both the V1 and V2 gathers read the drafter window `[c + 1, c + k + 1)`, which is ahead of `num_computed_tokens`. Once the target has passed an item, neither the target nor the drafter reads it again. Rejection rollback is still covered by `num_output_placeholders`. Async scheduling has the same timing as the existing non-spec path.
- **Stop at `start2`** instead of `start2 - L`, and only in the `can_allocate` failure branch. The drafter's read-ahead then lands on the item that isn't encoded yet. Both runners already handle that case: they fall back to token embeddings via the `start_pos >= computed + scheduled` check added in #46315. The `disable_chunked_mm_input` rollback still applies the shift.

Both changes are needed. Either one alone only narrows the hang condition from `gap < 2L` to `gap < L`.

**Tradeoff.** When the cache is full, the drafter uses token embeddings instead of image embeddings for up to `L` positions at that chunk boundary. This can slightly lower acceptance for one step. Requests whose items fit in the cache are unaffected.

**Relation to #59030.** #59030 adds a mid-schedule release of a request's consumed inputs, but it keeps the `+L` retention margin (its last commit re-added it). That release can never fire at this deadlock point, which is why its results match main in the sweep above. This PR instead argues that the margin isn't needed. The requeue half of #59030 is independent of this PR and complementary to it.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for analysis, the patch, tests, and running the validation. I reviewed every changed line and the results above.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Weight Cache] Key non-MoE DP daemons as DP=1 like the engine
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fixes #60178 . A dense (non-MoE) engine with `--data-parallel-size N` sends `dp_size=1, dp_rank=0` to the `vllm preload` daemon, which keys each rank as `dp_size=N, dp_rank=r`, so `--load-format ipc_cache` never maps the cached weights. The daemon now keys dense DP ranks as `(1, 0)` like the engine; MoE daemons are unchanged (follow-up to #57386).

## Claims

- A dense model with `--data-parallel-size N` and `--load-format ipc_cache` now maps its weights from the daemon on every rank.
- MoE daemons, daemons started without DP, and the per-GPU workaround from the issue are unchanged.
- No open PR touches the daemon's key. #59648 (`protocol.py`) and #59813 (`ipc_loader.py`) each add tests to `test_weight_cache.py`, a trivial rebase either way. #60006 rewrites `docs/features/preload.md` and keeps listing data parallelism as supported, which this fix makes true for dense models too.

## Validation

Unit test, no GPU needed:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_weight_cache.py -k "daemon or key or copy_mode" -q
```

`5 passed`. The new `test_daemon_keys_dense_dp_ranks_like_the_engine` checks that the daemon's key for a dense DP rank equals `ParallelConfig` after `reconfigure_for_independent_dp_rank()`, and that a MoE rank keeps `(dp_size, dp_rank)`.

End-to-end on 2x RTX A6000 with `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`, `main` at 5f30fc7031 vs this branch. Each scenario runs `vllm preload`, then `vllm serve --load-format ipc_cache`, then one greedy completion. "Map" means the worker logs `Mapped 339 tensors from the weight cache daemon`.

| | daemon | engine | before | after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | `-dp 2` | `-dp 2`, `fallback=false` | fails to start, `WeightCacheKey mismatch on fields: ['dp_size']` | 2/2 ranks map |
| B | `-dp 2` | `-dp 2`, default | 0/2 map, both ranks fall back to disk | 2/2 map |
| C | no DP | no DP | 1/1 map | 1/1 map |
| D | one no-DP daemon per GPU | `-dp 2` | 2/2 map | 2/2 map |

Every run that starts returns the same text before and after. `pre-commit` passes.

The unit test runs in the existing Model Executor CI step (`pytest model_executor`). The DP scenarios need two GPUs and a server, so they are not added to CI.

Not validated: TP > 1 with DP, multi-node DP, MoE with DP end to end, the Ray DP path, and draft daemons with DP.

## Details

Root cause:

1. For a non-MoE model, `run_engine_core` calls `reconfigure_for_independent_dp_rank()` on every DP rank, which sets `data_parallel_size = 1` and `data_parallel_rank = 0` ([`core.py` L1388-L1397](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/5f30fc7031cae49bf51073fc953d419b08f8887c/vllm/v1/engine/core.py#L1388-L1397)).
2. `IpcModelLoader` builds the key from `get_dp_group()`, so a dense engine sends `dp_size=1, dp_rank=0` on every GPU ([`ipc_loader.py` L345-L357](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/5f30fc7031cae49bf51073fc953d419b08f8887c/vllm/model_executor/model_loader/weight_cache/ipc_loader.py#L345-L357)).
3. `WeightCacheDaemon` used the launcher's `data_parallel_size` and its own `dp_rank` regardless of the model.

Fix: a new `get_engine_dp_placement(vllm_config, dp_rank)` in `daemon.py` returns `(1, 0)` when the target model is not MoE and `(dp_size, dp_rank)` otherwise. The daemon passes that to `WeightCacheKey.from_model_config`. It keys on the target model's `is_moe`, like `core.py`, so a draft daemon follows its target. It has one call site but stays a function so the test can compare it with `ParallelConfig.reconfigure_for_independent_dp_rank()` without constructing a daemon. Only the key changes; daemon placement and the world group are untouched.

All dense DP ranks now share one key. That is correct because they hold identical weights, and the per-GPU socket plus `_check_gpu_uuid` already bind each engine worker to the daemon on its own GPU.

Same class of bug as #56949 (RL weight transfer), where dense DP ranks also reset `data_parallel_rank` to 0.

---

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Sampler] Fix split top-p masking every token for huge logits (thinking_token_budget + spec decode emits token 0)
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

This affects `thinking_token_budget` with speculative decoding (MTP, on both the V1 runner and Model Runner V2) and any `top_p < 1`, including a model's `generation_config` default. When the budget is reached, the request emits token id 0 (`<unk>` for NemotronH) until `max_tokens` instead of the forced `</think>`. Greedy requests and `top_p=1.0` are not affected.

**Root cause.** The bug is in the split-row top-p pipeline (#54651), not in the thinking-budget code. `_topp_sb_mask_kernel` in `vllm/v1/sample/ops/topk_topp_triton.py` runs on CUDA for batches of 64 rows or fewer, for rows with top-p and without an active top-k. It finds its pivot in probability space but masks in logit space:

```python
pivot_logit = tl.log(pivot) + logZ + M
keep = x > pivot_logit
```

Thinking-budget forcing writes `1e9` into the end-of-reasoning logit. The V1 `ThinkingBudgetStateHolder` and the MRV2 `_thinking_budget_kernel` both do this, so `M = 1e9`. fp32 spacing at 1e9 is 64. The term `log(pivot) + log(Z)` (about -7.7) is lost in the addition, so `pivot_logit == M`. No token passes the strict `>`, and the whole row becomes `-inf`. From there:
- In the V1 rejection sampler, `softmax` gives NaN, the draft is rejected, and `sample_recovered_tokens_kernel` falls back to `recovered_id = 0`.
- In the MRV2 verifier (`_resample_kernel`), argmax over an all `-inf` row returns index 0.

Token 0 is sampled, the budget is still exceeded, forcing runs again, and the loop never ends. Throughput also drops about 3x because every draft is rejected.

Spec decode exposes the bug because the forced verification rows go through `apply_top_k_top_p`: V1 via `apply_sampling_constraints`, MRV2 via `SamplingStates.apply_top_k_top_p`. Non-spec decoding is safe only in the default configuration, where the fused FlashInfer sampler is used. If processed-logprobs mode is on, or the FlashInfer sampler is unavailable, non-spec sampling goes through the same Triton path and hits the same bug.

The monolithic `_topk_topp_kernel` (batches over 64) is left alone on purpose. Its `max_sample` estimate (avg + 10·std of a sample block) is far below 1e9, so `sum_exp` overflows to inf and the pivot becomes NaN. Its `not (final_pivot < max_logit)` guard then disables top-p for that row. Sampling stays correct because the 1e9 logit dominates the softmax.

**Fix.** Mask with the same probability-space predicate the step kernels used to measure the mass: `exp(x - M) / Z > pivot`. This matches `pivot` and `dup` bitwise against the values the search produced. Tie handling reuses the same `prob`; it already compared in probability space for exactly this precision reason. The row max is also kept as a backstop. For ordinary logits the kept set does not change: 24 of 24 randomized rows were identical before and after under `TRITON_INTERPRET=1`.

This is not a duplicate of #54906 or #39573. Those were reported on v0.28.1 and v0.19, which predate the split pipeline (#54651, 2026-09-03), and they describe the budget being ignored rather than token-0 output. No open PR or issue covers split top-p masking with large logits. #55414 touches the same kernel, but only to precompile variants.

## Known related follow-ups (out of scope)

- The monolithic `_topk_topp_kernel` has the same logit-space round trip (`final_pivot = log(p_pivot * sum_exp) + max_*`, `duplicate_logit = ...`). Today it fails open through the guard described above, so it does not produce wrong tokens.
- Thinking-budget forcing uses a `1e9` sentinel logit. Masking every other token to `-inf` and keeping the forced logit ("mask-and-bump") would stop producing extreme values that downstream sampling ops must tolerate.
- The `nomask = pivot * Z >= 1` guard in `_topp_sb_combine` is stale: pivots are always strictly below `hi = 1/Z`.
- Duplicate matching uses inconsistent tolerances: `abs(a - b) < 1e-9` in the step/combine kernels versus exact equality in the mask kernel.

## Test Plan

- New regression test `TestTritonTopkTopp::test_topp_keeps_forced_huge_logit` in `tests/v1/sample/test_topk_topp_sampler.py`:
  - batch sizes 4 and 64, both on the split path (64 is its maximum batch size);
  - forced logits `1e9` and `1e9/0.6` (the latter models temperature 0.6);
  - `p = 0.95`.
  
  It asserts that the forced logit survives, that every other token is masked (exactly one kept per row), that the softmax has no NaN, and that the argmax is the forced token.
- `pytest tests/v1/sample/test_topk_topp_sampler.py -v`
- CPU kernel repro under the Triton interpreter:
  - Harness: `topp_split_interp_harness.py`. It loads the kernel file with vLLM imports stubbed and drives `_topp_sb_stats_kernel`, `_topp_sb_step_kernel` and `_topp_sb_mask_kernel` exactly as `_apply_topp_split` does, with `num_sm=108` for A100.
  - Command:
    ```
    docker run --rm -v $PWD:/src python:3.12-slim sh -c "pip install -q --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu torch numpy && pip install -q triton==3.8.0 && mkdir -p /work && cp /src/topp_split_interp_harness.py /work/harness.py && TRITON_INTERPRET=1 V=131072 python /work/harness.py /src/vllm/v1/sample/ops/topk_topp_triton.py"
    ```
- End-to-end repro setup:
  - model: NemotronH-30B-A3B BF16 on 1x A100;
  - server flags: `--reasoning-parser nemotron_v3 --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":5}'`;
  - request: chat completion with `thinking_token_budget: 300`, `temperature: 1.0`, `logprobs: true`, `skip_special_tokens: false`.

## Related issues

- Related to #54906, but a different bug. #54906 reports the budget being ignored (reasoning continues) on MRV2 only, with `top_k=20` set. Rows with an active top-k go through the monolithic `_topk_topp_kernel`, not the split top-p path fixed here, so this PR is not expected to fix #54906.
- Same symptom family as #39573 (closed), which was reported on v0.19, before the split top-p pipeline (#54651) existed.

## Test Result

- CPU kernel under `TRITON_INTERPRET=1` (vocab 131072, p=0.95):
  - Before the fix, `forced 1e9` gives `kept=0`: the whole row is `-inf`, and sampling returns token 0 via NaN.
  - After the fix, `kept=1` (the forced token), and the sampled token is 13 (`</think>`).
  - Normal rows: 24 of 24 are identical to the pre-fix kernel, and within 1 token of the PyTorch sort reference.
- End-to-end on unpatched v0.30.0 (V1 runner + MTP5):
  - `top_p=0.95`: the budget is reached, then every remaining token is `<unk>`.
  - `top_p=1.0` or `top_k=50`: `</think>` is forced at the budget and a normal answer follows.
  - Greedy: works.
- GPU pytest (1x A100-SXM4-80GB, v0.30.0 with this fix applied, `--noconftest`):
  - `pytest tests/v1/sample/test_topk_topp_sampler.py -k test_topp_keeps_forced_huge_logit -v`: 4 passed (`split` and `split-boundary`, each with `1e9` and `1e9_over_temp0.6`).
  - `pytest tests/v1/sample/test_topk_topp_sampler.py`: 135 passed, 2 skipped, 0 failed. This includes the existing Triton and FlashInfer distribution and reference tests; `scipy` is needed for the FlashInfer distribution tests.
- Patched end-to-end run (MRV2, Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B + MTP `num_speculative_tokens=5`, 1x A100, default sampling `top_p=0.95`):
  - Raw `/v1/completions`, `thinking_token_budget=300`, `skip_special_tokens=false`: 0 `<unk>` tokens. `</think>` is forced at the budget and a valid JSON answer follows (`finish_reason=stop`). Checked on BF16 weights and on FP8 weights.
  - Chat, `thinking_token_budget=1000`: 212 tok/s (the unpatched run collapsed to 65 tok/s), `finish_reason=stop`, valid answer.
  - Not re-run on the V1 runner with the patch applied. The fix is in the shared Triton kernel that both runners call.

commits.pr_title: [Perf][DSv4.1] MegaAttn: wo_a writes wo_b's MXFP8 input
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

MegaAttn's (`FLASHMLA_MEGA_ATTN_DSV41`) `wo_a` einsum now writes `z` directly as MXFP8, together with the F8_128x4 UE8M0 scales that `wo_b`'s FlashInfer MXFP8 GEMM reads. `wo_b` therefore no longer quantizes a BF16 `z`, at any token count. It uses vllm-project/DeepGEMM#40 (merged), which adds the 128x4 scale layout to DeepGEMM's FP8 einsum epilogue. This PR bumps the DeepGEMM pin to it.

## Claims

- `_o_proj` drops the standalone `mxfp8_quantize` kernel. On GB200 it is 0.4-2.0 us per layer faster in decode (1-256 tokens) and 2.8-141 us faster in prefill (512-32768 tokens). The one regression is +0.6 us at 384 tokens (see Details).
- `wo_b` receives byte-identical FP8 data and scales, so model outputs do not change.
- Only `flash_mla_mega_attn.py` changes (+33/-5 lines vs main). Shared o_proj code and other backends are untouched.

## Validation

`_o_proj` alone (`wo_a` einsum, then `wo_b` CuTe-DSL MXFP8 GEMM) at DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash TP1 shapes: 8 groups x 4096 -> 1024, `wo_b` 8192 -> 5120. Setup: 1 x GB200, CUPTI, full CUDA graph, cold L2, median of 3 rounds, both arms in one process. Software: torch 2.13.0+cu132, FlashInfer 0.7.0.post1, DeepGEMM a7a9277 + DeepGEMM#40. Outputs are bitwise identical at all 20 sizes measured.

| tokens | main (us) | this PR (us) | delta (us) | main: einsum BF16 + quant (us) | PR: einsum FP8 (us) |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|

| 4 | 25.5 | 23.8 | -1.7 | 10.9 + 2.4 | 11.2 |
| 16 | 26.1 | 24.1 | -2.0 | 11.0 + 2.5 | 11.3 |
| 64 | 29.9 | 28.1 | -1.8 | 12.4 + 2.7 | 13.0 |
| 128 | 29.3 | 28.8 | -0.5 | 13.3 + 2.9 | 14.8 |
| 256 | 46.8 | 45.1 | -1.7 | 14.3 + 3.6 | 14.5 |
| 384 | 42.3 | 42.9 | +0.6 | 17.9 + 4.6 | 22.3 |
| 512 | 58.5 | 55.6 | -2.8 | 20.0 + 4.9 | 20.7 |
| 1024 | 77.7 | 73.2 | -4.5 | 33.4 + 7.7 | 34.1 |
| 4096 | 250.1 | 229.8 | -20.3 | 105.4 + 20.6 | 104.5 |
| 8192 | 497.4 | 454.5 | -42.9 | 216.8 + 36.2 | 210.5 |
| 16384 | 1010.0 | 906.5 | -103.5 | 439.5 + 68.2 | 430.4 |
| 32768 | 2127.5 | 1986.9 | -140.6 | 936.5 + 129.8 | 903.3 |

The previous revision of this PR wrote MN-major scales, swizzled them with a separate Triton kernel (1.6-5.2 us per call), and was gated to 1024+ tokens. The E2E prefill (DEP4) and accuracy results below were measured on that previous revision and were not re-run. This revision only removes the swizzle kernel from the same prefill path, and it hands `wo_b` the same bytes. Decode E2E has not been measured.

<details>
<summary>Previous revision: E2E prefill (DEP4, GB300) and accuracy</summary>

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, DEP4 (DP4 x TP1 + EP) on one GB300 node. Default config: SWA bounded replay on, MegaAttn, DeepGEMM mega MoE, fp8 KV cache, `max_num_batched_tokens=16384`, prefix caching off. Offline `LLM` per DP rank, one random-token prompt per rank, `max_tokens=1`. TTFT is measured from `scheduled_ts` to `first_token_ts` on the slowest rank; median of 3 repeats after a warmup.

| tokens/rank | base run 1 (ms) | base run 2 (ms) | PR (ms) | vs base mean |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1024 | 58.7 | 56.4 | 57.9 | +0.5% (noise) |
| 4096 | 93.1 | 92.9 | 91.4 | -1.7% |
| 8192 | 134.7 | 135.0 | 133.5 | -1.0% |
| 16384 | 229.1 | 227.9 | 227.4 | -0.5% |
| 32768 | 421.1 | 421.9 | 419.5 | -0.5% |

| eval | setup | score |
|---|---|---|
| GSM8K | lm-eval 0.4.13, 1319 problems, 5-shot, temperature 0, 4096-token cap, concurrency 32 | strict match 92.80%, flexible extract 92.72% (±0.7) |
| GPQA Diamond | gpt-oss `GPQAEval`, 198 problems, 0-shot chat, thinking on, temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95 | 89.90% (±2.1) |

</details>

Tests:
- vllm-project/DeepGEMM#40: all 7 tests in `tests/test_einsum.py` pass, including the new bitwise check of the 128x4 scales against the MN-major path.
- `tests/kernels/test_dsv41_mega_attn_layouts.py::test_quantized_o_proj_matches_quantized_bf16` now covers 1, 129 and 8193 tokens (decode, partial and multiple 128-row tiles), including CUDA graph capture and replay. It checks that `_o_proj`'s FP8 data and valid-row scales are byte-identical to `wo_b` quantizing the BF16 `z`. All 5 tests in the file pass on 1 x GB200 (torch 2.14.0+cu132, DeepGEMM with #40): `pytest tests/kernels/test_dsv41_mega_attn_layouts.py -v`.
- `pre-commit` (ruff, format, typos, shellcheck, mypy) passes.

## Details

- **Why the gate is gone.** DeepGEMM's einsum could only write MN-major packed scales, so `wo_b` needed a separate swizzle kernel. Below about 1024 tokens, that launch cost about as much as the quantization it saved. vllm-project/DeepGEMM#40 changes only the scale address in the einsum epilogue, so no extra kernel is left.
- **Gate conditions (unchanged).** The path runs when the einsum uses the per-32 recipe, `o_lora_rank % 128 == 0`, and `wo_b` is an MXFP8 kernel that accepts F8_128x4 scales (`can_fuse_query_quant`). It also requires no GEMM-RS, because the fused GEMM + reduce-scatter takes a BF16 `z` only.
- **Padded scale rows.** Rows past the last token in the final 128-row tile are not written. They only feed `wo_b` output rows that are never stored, so the test compares valid rows only.
- **384 tokens.** At 128-384 tokens (and at 2048 tokens), DeepGEMM's FP8-output einsum is slower than its BF16-output einsum, for example 17.9 -> 22.3 us at 384. The old MN-major scales show the same slowdown, so it is independent of this change. It is a DeepGEMM kernel-selection issue that can be fixed there.
- **DeepGEMM pin.** The pin points at `727f847`, the merge commit of DeepGEMM#40 on the fork's `dev` branch. The einsum selects the 128x4 scales with `use_128x4_sfd_layout=True`, which an older externally installed `deep_gemm` (vLLM prefers site-packages) does not accept.
- Merged `main` to resolve conflicts.

commits.pr_title: [Spec Decode][ROCm] Add FLy: entropy-gated deferred verification for draft-model speculative decoding
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

This PR adds [FLy](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.22972), an opt-in, lossy speculative verification policy, with support for both ModelRunner V1 and ModelRunner V2.

Standard verification stops at the first rejected draft token. FLy can accept an isolated rejection when the target entropy is high and the next `W` draft tokens all pass native verification. It needs no additional checkpoint or target forward pass. FLy does not preserve the target distribution and may reduce output quality; standard verification remains the default.

## Results at a glance

- **MRV2:** four recent models using DSpark/MTP, evaluated on AMD MI355X and NVIDIA B300. Across batch sizes 1, 4, 8, 16, 32, and 64, FLy improves decode throughput over Standard SD at all 48 model/platform/batch points: **1.055x–1.310x on AMD** and **1.041x–1.273x on NVIDIA**.
- **MRV2 quality:** Target / Standard SD / FLy comparisons on GSM8K, MATH-500, AIME25, and GPQA-Diamond. Minimum measured accuracy retention relative to Target is **96.43% on AMD** and **96.30% on NVIDIA**, both one-question differences on AIME25. These are single-pass measurements, not a quality guarantee.
- **V1:** the existing four target/draft pairs across ten benchmarks show **1.067x–1.938x** throughput versus Standard SD on AMD MI355X. Additional NVIDIA and non-zero-temperature results are retained below.

## Implementation

FLy changes verification decisions, using the native acceptance rule for each sampling mode: token equality for greedy target sampling, target-only acceptance for greedy drafting with random target sampling, or probability-ratio acceptance for probabilistic drafting.

A rejected position is eligible only when its draft token is not masked by target constraints, its top-k target entropy meets the threshold, and a full window of `W` subsequent draft tokens passes native verification. Another rejection within that window rejects the original position; a short trailing window is not deferred.

- **MRV1:** a pre-pass overrides the target argmax or uniform sample consumed by the existing acceptance kernels. The random path checks positive target and draft probability before forcing acceptance. Softmax is computed once and reused.
- **MRV2:** the rejection kernel tracks a pending rejection and commits the window only after all `W` native acceptances. Failed windows recover at the original rejected position, preserving that position's argmax or probability-normalization statistics.

Entropy is computed from processed target scores as `-sum(p * log(p))` over the largest `fly_entropy_top_k` probabilities, without renormalizing that subset. The default top-k is 3. This is the implementation's top-k gate, rather than the paper's full-vocabulary normalized entropy.

Configuration validates the window and logs a one-time lossy-method warning. Probabilistic drafting retains draft probabilities for FLy. The V1 pre-pass uses int64 vocabulary-offset arithmetic to avoid overflow on large batches.

This PR also rejects `use_heterogeneous_vocab=True` together with `use_local_argmax_reduction=True`: the local-argmax path otherwise bypasses vocabulary intersection and token-ID mapping. This validation applies to all verification methods. FLy-specific entropy and acceptance work runs only when explicitly enabled.

## Usage

```python
from vllm import LLM

llm = LLM(
    model="Qwen/Qwen3-8B",
    speculative_config={
        "method": "draft_model",
        "model": "Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B",
        "num_speculative_tokens": 8,
        "rejection_sample_method": "fly",
        "fly_window_size": 6,
        "fly_entropy_threshold": 0.3,
        "fly_entropy_top_k": 3,
    },
)
```

`fly_window_size` defaults to `min(6, num_speculative_tokens - 1)`. FLy requires at least two speculative tokens and a window smaller than that count. `fly_entropy_top_k` must be positive and is capped at the vocabulary size.

FLy supports heterogeneous vocabularies through the existing token mapping with greedy drafting. The proposer allowlist has been removed; `extract_hidden_states` is explicitly rejected because it does not perform speculative verification.

Standalone `draft_model` proposing uses MRV1. MRV2 supports FLy with its supported proposers, including MTP and DSpark as evaluated below. FLy does not force a fallback to MRV1. The MRV2 measurements use `fly_window_size=2`, as specified in their setup.

## ModelRunner V2 evaluation

All runs use ModelRunner V2 and the models' native speculative heads. Draft sampling is greedy. FLy uses `window=2`, a default entropy threshold of `0.3`, and entropy top-k `3`.

Target-only (`T`) is the primary quality reference, while Standard SD (`SD`) is included as a sanity baseline. `FLy−T` is the absolute accuracy difference, and retention is `FLy correct / Target correct`.

`T` / `SD` / `FLy` denote target-only decoding, standard speculative decoding and FLy. ## Limitations

- FLy is intentionally lossy. The measured quality differences include regressions and do not establish distribution preservation or a general accuracy bound.
- The MRV2 quality runs are single pass@1 measurements, with only 30 AIME25 problems. No recent-model TerminalBench, SWE-bench Pro, or HLE result is included in this update; the HLE results in the V1 tables use older models.
- Runner/proposer compatibility still applies: standalone `draft_model` proposing requires MRV1, and FLy is not supported on CPU. Heterogeneous-vocabulary drafting requires greedy draft sampling and cannot use local argmax reduction.
- Model evaluations reported here were not rerun after the latest rebase and index-width fix; local regression and large-offset checks are listed below.

## Why this is not a duplicate

FLy changes the accept/reject decision and is intentionally lossy. This differs from verification-budget approaches such as [#47808](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/47808) and [#47131](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/47131), and from the similarly named [DFly drafting proposal](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50246). The open-PR title search for FLy on September 25 returned only this PR.

## Tests

Before the index-width fix, both complete sampler suites passed (**157 tests**):

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/sample/test_rejection_sampler.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_rejection_sampler_utils.py -q
```

After the fix, the affected V1 FLy tests passed (**7 tests**):

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/sample/test_rejection_sampler.py -k fly -q
```

Direct GPU checks exercised vocabulary offsets above `2**31` in the greedy, target-only random, and probabilistic `p/q` pre-passes, including masked-token rejection. All passed, and generated Triton IR confirmed int64 vocabulary-offset multiplications.

The added configuration tests were removed following review; sampler and kernel behavior tests remain. Changed-file pre-commit checks passed, including Ruff, Markdown lint, and mypy.

## Attribution

This work was done at AMD and the primary evaluation ran on AMD Instinct MI355X. AI assistance was used for this change (recorded as Assisted-by: in the commit trailer). I have reviewed every changed line and ran the tests and evaluations above myself.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Fix auto truncation without an output token limit
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fix automatic prompt truncation in Chat Completions and Responses when no output token limit is specified. Previously, truncation could fill the entire context window, leaving no room for generation and causing requests to fail.

## Claims

- Reserve one token for generation when automatic truncation is enabled without an explicit output limit.
- Preserve existing behavior for explicit output limits and zero-output budgets.
- Keep pooling requests able to use the full input context.

## Validation

Added regression tests covering text and token-ID prompts, Chat serving, and unspecified, zero, and positive output budgets.

Validated with `DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B` (`max_model_len=512`):

| Request | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Chat, output limit omitted | HTTP 400: `max_tokens` is 0 | HTTP 200 |
| Responses, output limit omitted | HTTP 400: prompt fills context | HTTP 200 |

Both requests produced 511 input tokens and 1 output token after the fix. Requests with explicit output limits remained unchanged.

- **54 tests passed**.
- All applicable pre-commit checks passed, including mypy.

```bash
pytest -q \
  tests/renderers/test_completions.py \
  tests/entrypoints/openai/responses/test_sampling_params.py \
  tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_serving_chat.py::test_serving_chat_mistral_token_ids_prompt_is_validated \
  tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_serving_chat.py::test_serving_chat_mistral_token_ids_prompt_too_long_is_rejected
```

## Details

Both request protocols converted an unspecified output limit from `None` to `0` when constructing `TokenizeParams`. Automatic truncation interpreted this as a zero-output budget, allowing the prompt to fill the entire context window.

Preserve `None` for unspecified output limits so automatic truncation reserves one token for generation. Keep the `TokenizeParams` default at `0` to preserve behavior for callers that do not generate output.

---

commits.pr_title: [Feature][PCP] Support APC and encoder-side SWA bounded replay for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Follow up on #59857 to enable automatic prefix caching (APC) together with encoder-side SWA bounded replay for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash under PCP in a colocated model instance. The initial PCP implementation rejected APC; this change enables the PCP + APC + encoder-side replay combination.

## Claims

- Enable local APC prefix hits under PCP and rebuild the SWA tail through encoder-side bounded replay while preserving cached compressed KV and indexer keys across ranks.
- Decoder-side tail trimming remains disabled under PCP; scheduled rows execute the normal decoder layers.

## Validation

### Environment

- Model: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash
- Hardware: two separate nodes, each with 8x NVIDIA H20 97,871 MiB; driver 535.161.08
- Image: `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-49cb2bbf71cfd36ee5aa33d1e184b1cddff55294`
- Baseline: the image + prerequisite #59857
- Candidate: the same image and prerequisite + This PR; APC and bounded replay were enabled.
- Common topology: TP2/PCP4, PP1, DCP1, Humming MoE, eager execution, and synchronous scheduling.

Candidate launch command:

```bash
python -m vllm.entrypoints.cli.main serve /models/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 18001 \
  --served-model-name deepseek-v4.1-flash \
  --language-model-only \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \
  --attention-backend FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV41 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla \
  --block-size 64 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 \
  --pipeline-parallel-size 1 \
  --decode-context-parallel-size 1 \
  --prefill-context-parallel-size 4 \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --all2all-backend allgather_reducescatter \
  --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true}' \
  --moe-backend humming \
  --max-model-len auto \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 \
  --max-num-seqs 64 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --enable-prefix-caching \
  --swa-bounded-replay \
  --enforce-eager \
  --no-async-scheduling
```

Baseline used the same command except:

```bash
  --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --no-swa-bounded-replay
```

### Prefix-repetition performance

Both arms ran concurrently with byte-identical deterministic inputs:

```bash
vllm bench serve \
  --backend openai \
  --base-url http://<HOST>:18001 \
  --endpoint /v1/completions \
  --model deepseek-v4.1-flash \
  --tokenizer /tmp/dsv41-tokenizer \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \
  --dataset-name prefix_repetition \
  --prefix-repetition-prefix-len 1024 \
  --prefix-repetition-suffix-len 128 \
  --prefix-repetition-num-prefixes 10 \
  --prefix-repetition-output-len 1 \
  --num-prompts 80 \
  --num-warmups 8 \
  --request-rate inf \
  --max-concurrency 8 \
  --seed 42 \
  --temperature 0 \
  --ignore-eos \
  --percentile-metrics ttft,e2el \
  --disable-tqdm
```

| Metric | Baseline | Candidate | Delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Successful requests | 80/80 | 80/80 | - |
| Mean TTFT | 640.73 ms | 386.73 ms | **-39.64%** |
| Median TTFT | 570.56 ms | 346.28 ms | **-39.31%** |
| P99 TTFT | 907.04 ms | 712.10 ms | **-21.49%** |
| Effective input throughput | 13,837.87 tok/s | 22,499.21 tok/s | **+62.59%** |
| Request throughput | 12.01 req/s | 19.53 req/s | **+62.59%** |
| Prefix-cache token hit ratio | disabled | 80,384/101,376 (79.29%) | - |

Every measured request had exactly 1,152 input tokens and one output token. There were no failed requests or Pod restarts.

### Full GSM8K

Both arms ran the same full 1,319-sample ModelScope test split:

```bash
evalscope eval \
  --eval-type openai_api \
  --api-url http://<HOST>:18001/v1 \
  --api-key EMPTY \
  --model deepseek-v4.1-flash \
  --model-id deepseek-v4.1-flash \
  --datasets gsm8k \
  --dataset-hub modelscope \
  --dataset-args '{"gsm8k":{"few_shot_num":4}}' \
  --seed 42 \
  --eval-batch-size 64 \
  --generation-config '{"temperature":0.0,"top_p":1.0,"max_tokens":8192,"reasoning_effort":"high","seed":42,"timeout":10000}' \
  --timeout 10000
```

EvalScope version: 1.11.1.

| Metric | Baseline | Candidate |
|---|---:|---:|
| Accuracy | 1279/1319 (96.97%) | 1284/1319 (97.35%) |
| API errors | 0 | 0 |

Paired outcomes were 1,277 both correct, 33 both wrong, 7 candidate-only correct, and 2 baseline-only correct. The exact two-sided McNemar p-value was `0.1797`, so the observed `+0.38 pp` accuracy difference is not statistically significant. Candidate GSM8K traffic recorded 674,816/803,206 local prefix-cache hit tokens (84.02%).

## Details

Reuse the existing scheduler replay boundary and padding kernel, stage replay starts per local PCP segment, mask each rank's own cacheable slots, and gather those slots back in the same rank-major order as KV publication. All ranks participate even when a peer has no replay rows; SWA and compressor scratch mappings stay unchanged. The additional slot metadata collective applies only to PCP batches with encoder replay enabled. Production changes are confined to DeepSeek-V4.1 files, with the existing non-PCP path and other PCP restrictions retained.

This does not duplicate #61554, which targets cold-prefill decoder trimming with prefix caching disabled. Enable APC and encoder-side replay with `--enable-prefix-caching --swa-bounded-replay`. The supported scope is NVIDIA CUDA, MRV2, eager execution, synchronous scheduling and PP=DP=DCP=1. KV connectors, speculative decoding, microbatching and MegaMoE remain unsupported with PCP. AI assistance was used for implementation and Codex CLI review; human line-by-line review remains pending, while GPU/model validation is documented above.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Honor --enable-log-outputs on /v1/completions
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`--enable-log-outputs` is silently ignored by `/v1/completions`. The handler never accepted the flag or logged generated text, while chat, Responses, Anthropic (#60982), Cohere (#61089) and `/inference/v1/generate` all do. This adds output logging to completions, mirroring chat.

## Claims

- With `--enable-log-requests --enable-log-outputs`, `/v1/completions` logs generated text: one line per output when not streaming; when streaming, one line per delta (respects `--enable-log-deltas`) plus the full text when the stream ends.
- Output lines reuse the per-prompt request id from the input log (`cmpl-<id>-<i>`), so the two can be correlated.
- Nothing changes when the flag is off (the default).

## Validation

**End-to-end,** `vllm serve Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct --enable-log-requests --enable-log-outputs` (CPU backend). For each request, the counts of `Received request` / `Generated response` log lines:

| Request | `main` | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| `/v1/completions`, non-streaming | 1 / **0** | 1 / **1** |
| `/v1/completions`, streaming, 8 tokens | 1 / **0** | 1 / **9** (8 deltas + complete) |
| `/v1/chat/completions` (control) | 1 / 1 | 1 / 1 |

<details>
<summary>Log lines with this PR</summary>

```
Generated response cmpl-e2e-cmpl-nonstream-0: output: ' Paris. It was founded in 7', finish_reason: length
Generated response cmpl-e2e-cmpl-stream-0 (streaming delta): output: ' Paris', finish_reason: None
Generated response cmpl-e2e-cmpl-stream-0 (streaming delta): output: '.', finish_reason: None
...
Generated response cmpl-e2e-cmpl-stream-0 (streaming delta): output: '7', finish_reason: length
Generated response cmpl-e2e-cmpl-stream-0 (streaming complete): output: ' Paris. It was founded in 7', finish_reason: streaming_complete
Generated response chatcmpl-e2e-chat-nonstream: output: 'Hello! How can I assist you today', finish_reason: length
```
</details>

**Tests:** `test_completion_logs_outputs_when_enabled[stream=False|True]` drives `create_completion` with a mock engine and checks the logged text, token ids, finish reason, delta/complete lines, and that every line uses the input log's request id.

```
$ pytest tests/entrypoints/openai/completion/test_completion_error.py tests/entrypoints/openai/completion/test_completion_text_offset.py
main:    2 failed, 51 passed  (TypeError: ... unexpected keyword argument 'enable_log_outputs')
this PR: 53 passed
```

Regression: `pytest tests/entrypoints/openai/completion/{test_completion_error,test_completion_text_offset,test_lora_resolvers}.py tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_serving_chat.py tests/entrypoints/serve/utils`: `main` 279 passed, this PR 281 passed. Both have the same 19 environment-only failures (GPT-OSS/Harmony tokenizers unavailable offline). `pre-commit` ruff and mypy are clean.

Validated on macOS (Apple Silicon, CPU backend), Python 3.12, torch 2.14.0, rebased on `main` @ `e744eacf6`. No model evaluation: logging only.

## Details

commits.pr_title: [Core] Reject new requests while generation is paused
commits.pr_body:
Addresses the second problem in #51476. Redesigned per @hao-aaron's review: the engine, not each frontend, is the source of truth for pause admission.

Builds on #59559, now merged.

## Purpose

`pause_generation(mode="abort"|"wait")` and `sleep()` treat the pause as a generation boundary, but requests arriving afterwards were silently queued in the paused engine and then served after resume, under the new weights.

## Contract

- Once `pause_generation(abort|wait)` returns, and until `resume_generation()` returns, new requests from **every** API server sharing the engine fail with `EnginePausedError` (HTTP 503, retryable). `keep` still accepts and queues them.
- A request racing the pause call itself may be rejected or treated as in-flight. It never hangs and never leaves residue.
- A paused engine (`abort`/`wait`) accepts no input except KV-transfer cleanup markers. A streaming-input session's next input is rejected the same way, which ends the session in the engine and on the client.

## Change

- **Engine admission.** `_reject_add_while_paused` runs next to `_reject_add_in_shutdown`, before `add_request`, so a rejected add never reaches the scheduler or DP wave state. It rejects only in `PAUSED_NEW` (abort/wait), and lets `abort_immediately` markers through so P/D KV cleanup still runs. The rejection also ends any open streaming session under the rejected id, since the client treats a rejected id as finished. The busy loop handles ADDs and pause/resume serially, so no lock is needed.
- **Surfacing.** New `FinishReason.PAUSED`. `OutputProcessor` finishes the rejected child like any finished request and raises `EnginePausedError` (a `GracefulHTTPError`, 503) to its caller. `generate` then aborts the request, reclaiming `n>1` siblings; it only does so after the fan-out is fully sent, so no child can slip in untracked after a resume. The Rust frontend maps it to a 503 (`engine_paused`) in `/v1/completions`, `/v1/chat/completions` and `/inference/v1/generate`, and to `UNAVAILABLE` over gRPC.
- **Rejected streaming and pooling requests.** A rejected streaming-input session stops taking input (its input task is cancelled), whoever reads its collector, and any chunk its input task sent after the rejection is aborted in the engine. Under DP load balancing that abort follows main's `streaming_reqs` routing (#58942), so an open session's abort reaches every engine even after the rejection retired its route. A rejected pooling request no longer hits a generation-only assert: `AsyncLLM.encode` raises `EnginePausedError`, and the sync `LLMEngine` over multiprocessing gets an empty result.
- **DP.** With rejection alone, the frontend's `FIRST_REQ` for a rejected request would leave it believing a wave was running, and the first request after resume hung in the DP collective (Python and standalone Rust frontends alike). #59559 removed the frontend wake altogether: engines alone start waves, so this PR needs no DP-specific change.
The previous revision's client-side admission flag, control-plane lock and reopen logic are removed.

The scheduler is not touched, and `ABORT` handling and sleep/resume behave as on main.

## Known limitations

- `wait` behaves as on main for requests admitted before the pause: running ones finish, but ones still queued (or preempted during the drain) stay queued and run after resume. Draining them too needs a scheduler change, left to a follow-up PR on top of this one.
- `stream=true` HTTP requests receive the 503 as an SSE error chunk, because the rejection arrives after the response has started.
- The sync `LLMEngine` over multiprocessing returns `finish_reason="paused"` rather than raising. The in-process engine (`VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING=0`) has no API server in front of it and still queues requests while paused, as on main.
- Closing a streaming-input session's input while paused: an idle session closes normally (the client completes it and the engine ends it). A session closed while its chunk is still running under `wait` fails with a 503 rather than finishing that chunk.
- As on main, `wait` with `clear_cache=True` fails the cache reset while an idle streaming session holds KV.

## Test Plan

- `test_engine_core.py`: engine-side rejection per pause state ends any open session under the rejected id, and KV cleanup markers pass.
- `test_output_processor.py`: a paused rejection finishes cleanly for generate and pooling, sync and async, and stops a streaming session's input.
- `test_async_llm.py`: admission per mode through a direct collector (`n=2`, no residue, `keep` proven to reach the paused engine); a pause mid `n>1` fan-out reclaims a sibling the pause left queued.
- `test_async_llm_dp.py`: the late-request drain tests also assert rejection and no residue, and that the next request after resume completes.
- `test_pause_multi_frontend.py` (new): with `--api-server-count 2`, all 32 requests after `/pause` get 503 and all succeed after `/resume`.
- Rust `routes/tests.rs`: a paused rejection is an `engine_paused` error on every route that maps it: a 503 from `/v1/completions`, `/v1/chat/completions` and non-streaming `/inference/v1/generate`, and an SSE error from streaming `/inference/v1/generate`.

## Test Result

All runs inside `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` (af7f9488c) with the PR files bind-mounted, `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B` / `ibm-research/PowerMoE-3b`, on H200. GPUs were shared with another job; a test that failed at engine start-up on memory was rerun alone.

| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| New unit tests (engine core, output processor, DP LB client, plus #59559's wave announce; run before the DP LB abort test was dropped for main's #58942 routing) | 14 passed |
| Pause tests in `test_async_llm.py` | 10 passed |
| HTTP: multi-frontend + RLHF pause lifecycle (MRV1/MRV2 × abort/wait/keep) | 7 passed |
| `test_scheduler.py`, `test_async_scheduler.py`, `test_output_processor.py`, `admission_control`, `streaming_input/` | 306 passed (plus the 4 above); 9 fail identically without this PR or need >1 GPU |
| Full `test_async_llm.py`, streaming-input e2e, RLHF suite | 55 passed; 7 are the vision model failing engine init under the shared-GPU memory cap |
| Full `test_async_llm_dp.py`, mp + ray (incl. #59559's repro) | 28 passed, 4 skipped |
| DP=2 MoE, `--api-server-count 2`: six pause/resume cycles (abort/wait/keep) under load, then sleep/wake | rejected while paused, all served after resume |
| Rust `vllm-engine-core-client` and `vllm-server` | 132 and 469 passed |
| `vllm-rs serve` (standalone and bootstrapped) + DP (MoE, 2 ranks): request rejected while paused, then resume | next request completes |

Mutation checks: reverting only the same-id session end at the gate, the client-side streaming end, or the `generate` sibling abort makes its test fail; breaking the `Paused` mapping in any one of the four Rust route cases fails the Rust route test.

## Essential Elements

- Not a duplicate: supersedes this PR's earlier client-side design. #51487 is the conservative counterpart.
- Control-plane and scheduling only, no effect on model output; no eval run.
- AI assistance was used (Claude, with Codex, Kimi K3 and Claude Fable as independent adversarial reviewers). The submitter reviewed every changed line and the runs above.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][ROCm][MoRIIO] Support heterogeneous TP in WRITE mode for all attention and mamba layers
commits.pr_body:
Fixes #60101. This PR fixes a hang in MoRIIO WRITE-mode disaggregated serving when using MLA models with a smaller tensor-parallel size on prefill than on decode.

For example, with prefill TP2 and decode TP4, the expected mapping is:

- Prefill rank 0 → decode ranks 0 and 1
- Prefill rank 1 → decode ranks 2 and 3

Previously, each prefill rank wrote the KV cache to only the first mapped decode rank. The other decode ranks did not receive their KV cache or completion notification and continued waiting indefinitely.

## Root cause

MoRIIO already calculated the first corresponding remote TP rank, but the WRITE data path treated this as a one-to-one mapping.

That behavior is sufficient for equal TP sizes and mappings that do not require replication. However, the MLA KV cache must be fanned out when the decode TP size is a multiple of and larger than the prefill TP size.

The existing heterogeneous-TP acknowledgement logic expects completion from all corresponding decode ranks, while the WRITE path previously reached only one of them.

## Changes

This PR introduces a small helper, `get_moriio_write_target_tp_ranks`, which extends the existing remote-rank mapping for MLA WRITE fan-out.

When MLA is used and decode TP is larger than prefill TP:

1. Determine the first decode rank using the existing MoRIIO TP-rank mapping.
2. Calculate the required fan-out from the prefill and decode TP sizes.
3. Establish sessions with every corresponding decode rank.
4. Write the KV cache through every target session.
5. Wait for all resulting transfer statuses before completing the request.
6. Send `write_done` to every target decode rank.
7. Send `write_failed` to every affected target if a deferred write times out.

## Scope and compatibility

The fan-out behavior is restricted to:

- MoRIIO WRITE mode
- MLA models
- Prefill TP smaller than decode TP

This change is contained within the vLLM MoRIIO connector and does not require changes to the MoRI library.

Routing is based on TP/DP ranks and the existing endpoint-resolution logic rather than physical node placement. Runtime validation was performed on a single node.

## Unit tests

Added coverage for:

- MLA TP2 → TP4 target mapping
- MLA TP4 → TP8 target mapping
- Equal and decreasing TP mappings
- Non-MLA behavior remaining unchanged
- Creating a write session for every fan-out target
- Accumulating all transfer statuses
- Sending completion notifications to every target
- Sending timeout/failure notifications to every target
- Passing fan-out routing information from the connector to the writer
- Existing DP and multi-pod notification behavior

commits.pr_title: [CPU][Bugfix] Flatten >2-D activations in the AMX int8 W8A8 linear path
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fixes #61964.

On AMX CPUs, `CPUInt8ScaledMMLinearKernel` routes symmetric W8A8 linears with aligned shapes to `_apply_weights_sgl` (the SGLang-derived `int8_scaled_mm_with_quant` kernel), which has been the default since #50801. That path passes activations straight to the kernel, and the kernel enforces `CHECK_DIM(2, mat1)`. The Whisper encoder runs on `B x T x D`, so W8A8 Whisper fails on AMX machines with `RuntimeError: mat1 must be a 2D tensor`. Non-AMX CPUs fall back to `_apply_weights_onednn`, which already flattens to `[M, K]` and restores the leading dims, so the model works there.

This PR applies the same flatten/reshape in `_apply_weights_sgl`. It matches `_apply_weights_onednn` and `CPUFp8BlockScaledMMKernel` in the same file, and the W4A16 fix in #58268. 2-D inputs (all decoder-only models) are unaffected.

**Not a duplicate:** I searched open PRs and issues for `_apply_weights_sgl`, `int8_scaled_mm_with_quant`, and CPU/Whisper W8A8. The only related item is #56029, which fixes the ROCm Triton `scaled_mm` path (#56024) and doesn't touch the CPU kernel.

## Test Plan

- New unit test `test_cpu_sgl_int8_linear_accepts_3d_input` in `tests/kernels/quantization/test_scaled_mm_kernel_selection.py` (already a `cpu_test` file). It builds a layer through `CPUInt8ScaledMMLinearKernel.process_weights_for_sgl`, runs `apply_weights` on a `[2, 3, K]` input, and checks the result is bit-identical to the flattened `[6, K]` call reshaped back. The test is skipped when `int8_scaled_mm_with_quant` is not built.
- `pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_scaled_mm_kernel_selection.py -v`
- `pre-commit run --files <changed files>`

## Test Result

Run on an AVX512-BF16 host (AMD EPYC 9454). It loads the same `_C` library, so the SGL int8 op runs there through its non-AMX fallback.

- Without the fix, the new test fails with `RuntimeError: mat1 must be a 2D tensor`.
- With the fix:

```text
tests/kernels/quantization/test_scaled_mm_kernel_selection.py  11 passed
```

- pre-commit: all hooks passed (ruff check, ruff format, typos, mypy, SPDX, test tethering, ...).

I don't currently have AMX hardware available, so I haven't run an end-to-end W8A8 Whisper accuracy check on GNR/SPR. The change only affects inputs that previously raised, and the 2-D path is unchanged. I'd appreciate an AMX run from CPU CI or reviewers (cc @bigPYJ1151).

*AI assistance was used to prepare this change. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.*

## Overview

Fix Python DeepSeek V4.1 rendering when tool results reorder image placeholders or thinking mode drops historical developer content. Carry source image indices through the native encoder and apply the resulting order to both image data and UUIDs.

This follows the source-order approach of #56366, which fixed the Rust frontend only.

- Images belonging to dropped developer content no longer reach multimodal prompt expansion without a placeholder.

commits.pr_title: [Frontend] Raise VLLMValidationError for an unknown Harmony channel in Responses output parsing
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fixes #58384 (partially, see "Not addressed" below).

`vllm/entrypoints/openai/responses/harmony.py::_parse_message_no_recipient` raises a bare `ValueError("Unknown channel: <x>")` when gpt-oss emits a Harmony message on a channel outside `analysis` / `commentary` / `final` (seen in production as `comment`; #22533 reported `commentaryanalysis`). Per review, this PR keeps that behaviour and raises `VLLMValidationError` instead, consistent with the other `VLLMValidationError` raises in the same module, so the error is classified as a vLLM client-side error rather than an unexpected exception.

## Change

- `vllm/entrypoints/openai/responses/harmony.py` (+1/-1): `raise ValueError(...)` -> `raise VLLMValidationError(...)` (the import already exists).
- `tests/entrypoints/openai/responses/test_harmony_utils.py` (+8): `test_unknown_channel_raises_validation_error`, parametrized over `comment` / `commentaryanalysis`, through `harmony_to_response_output` (the entry point `serving.py` uses).

An earlier revision dropped such messages instead of raising; it was replaced following the review discussion.

## Not addressed

For `stream=true`, the raise still happens when `responses_stream_generator` assembles the final response after the deltas were delivered, so the SSE stream still ends without `response.completed`. Happy to follow up separately (for example emitting a `response.failed` / error event there) if maintainers want that.

## Duplicate-work check

`gh` searches of vllm-project/vllm issues and PRs (all states) for "Unknown channel", "harmony channel", "harmony_to_response_output", "_parse_message_no_recipient": #22533 and #22578 (closed stale, same symptom), no open PR changes this raise; #35906 / #35907 touch the same file but not this line.

## Test Plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/entrypoints/openai/responses/test_harmony_utils.py
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/entrypoints/openai/responses/test_harmony_utils.py -k unknown_channel   # before / after
ruff check / ruff format --check on the two changed files
```

commits.pr_title: [CPU] Fix underflow in FP8 AMX attention
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fix underflow in CPU FP8 AMX attention with BF16 exponent lifting and delayed scale compensation, plus cache writes that avoid tiny FP32 intermediates. Follow-up to #39445.

## Claims

- AMX decoding retains FTZ with **four instead of six** vector conversion instructions per 32 values.
- E4M3/E5M2 attention latency: **5.4% lower** than the original decoder across six workloads per format.

## Validation

### Model evaluation

GSM8K results are from earlier decoder comparisons; FTZ rows precede delayed scaling (`da46b8b`).

RedHatAI/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-quantized.w8a8, BF16 compute, all 1,319 GSM8K questions, 5-shot, chat template, seed 42, greedy decoding, maximum 512 generated tokens, batch size 32, prefix caching disabled.

| KV format / decoder | Flexible extract | Strict match |
|---|---:|---:|
| E4M3, original underflow-prone | 77.786% | 73.995% |
| E4M3, exact-subnormal alternative | 83.245% | 81.804% |
| E4M3, FTZ before delayed scaling | 83.017% | 79.757% |
| E5M2, proper-subnormal integer alternative | 80.667% | 78.772% |
| E5M2, FTZ before delayed scaling | 81.804% | 78.999% |

All runs passed sample-count validation; prompt, target, and document hashes match within each comparison.

```bash
MODEL=RedHatAI/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-quantized.w8a8
KV_DTYPE=fp8_e4m3  # Repeat with fp8_e5m2.
MODEL_ARGS="pretrained=$MODEL,dtype=bfloat16,kv_cache_dtype=$KV_DTYPE,seed=42"
MODEL_ARGS+=",max_model_len=4096,max_num_seqs=32,max_num_batched_tokens=8192"
MODEL_ARGS+=",enable_prefix_caching=false,enforce_eager=true,kv_cache_memory_bytes=17179869184"

VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING=0 lm_eval run \
  --model vllm --model_args "$MODEL_ARGS" \
  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --batch_size 32 \
  --apply_chat_template --seed 42 \
  --gen_kwargs temperature=0,max_gen_toks=512 \
  --log_samples --output_path "gsm8k_$KV_DTYPE"
```

### Kernel validation and performance

- Full CPU build and pre-commit passed.
- Eight targeted attention regressions passed, covering encoded subnormals, split reduction, and large cache scales.
- 28 attention behavior checks passed, including split/unsplit, sliding window, softcap, ALiBi, sinks, and VEC.
- All 256 byte encodings of each format were checked against the selected conversion contract with FTZ/DAZ enabled and disabled.

Production assembly confirms four vector conversion instructions per 32 values for E4M3/E5M2 at head sizes 128 and 256.

Three balanced rounds; five repetitions of 20 timed calls per workload. Workload medians pool 15 repetitions; ratios are geometric means across six workloads per format.

| Attention comparison | E4M3 | E5M2 | Combined |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| This PR / original underflow-prone decoder | 0.9525 | 0.9402 | 0.9463 |
| This PR / delayed scaling without FTZ | 1.0248 | 1.0019 | 1.0133 |

Combined ratios by round were 0.9570/0.9435/0.9415 versus original and 1.0222/1.0039/1.0043 versus delayed scaling without FTZ. BF16 controls were within 0.2% overall; the small latter gap is subject to timing variation. These are kernel timings, not end-to-end serving speedups.

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu uv pip install -e . -v --no-build-isolation

.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_cpu_attn.py \
  -k 'fp8_qk_covers_full_64_token_group or fp8_large_prefill_amx' -q

# Representative large-prefill benchmark.
.venv/bin/python benchmarks/kernels/cpu/benchmark_cpu_attn.py \
  --isa amx --dtype bfloat16 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e5m2 \
  --batch-size 1 --q-len-min 512 --q-len-max 512 \
  --kv-len-min 4096 --kv-len-max 4096 \
  --head-size 128 --num-query-heads 32 --num-kv-heads 8 \
  --block-size 128 --num-blocks 32 --iters 20
```

The existing pytest selection above passed one case and skipped one. The additional reproducers and conversion checks were run locally; no new tests or benchmark files are added to CI.

## Details

The old decoder scaled BF16 values by `2^-120`/`2^-112`; AMX flushed small operands/products before the later scale correction could recover them.

Both AMX decoders lift normal values by `2^8`/`2^16`, compensated in K/V scales, and flush encoded FP8 subnormals to zero. NaN/Inf correction is omitted because the cache writer saturates inputs to finite FP8 codes.

Open-PR searches for CPU FP8 attention and AMX underflow found no overlapping fix.

AI assistance was used for implementation, validation, source and assembly review, and drafting.
