commits.pr_title: [BugFix][MyPy] Guard Linux-only mmap/fadvise calls with sys.platform
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

`mmap.MADV_HUGEPAGE`, `os.posix_fadvise` and `os.POSIX_FADV_DONTNEED` are
Linux-only. On macOS, mypy fails with:

```text
vllm/model_executor/model_loader/weight_utils.py:923: error: Module has no attribute "posix_fadvise"  [attr-defined]
vllm/model_executor/model_loader/weight_utils.py:923: error: Module has no attribute "POSIX_FADV_DONTNEED"  [attr-defined]
vllm/models/deepseek_v41/common/engram.py:911: error: Module has no attribute "MADV_HUGEPAGE"  [attr-defined]
```

At runtime the same lines raise `AttributeError`, which the surrounding
`except OSError` does not catch.

This PR adds a `sys.platform != "linux"` early return so that non-Linux
platforms take the existing fallbacks:

- `_allocate_huge_page_storage` returns `None`, so the caller falls back to
  pinned memory.
- `drop_checkpoint_cache` skips page-cache eviction.

mypy understands `sys.platform` checks, so the Linux-only code is no longer
type-checked on macOS. This follows the same approach as #41465.

Both call sites were introduced in #56926.

## Duplicate check

I searched open PRs for `posix_fadvise`, `MADV_HUGEPAGE` and `mypy sys.platform`.
None of the open PRs guards these calls or fixes the macOS mypy errors.

## Test Plan

On macOS (darwin, arm64):

```bash
pre-commit run mypy --files vllm/models/deepseek_v41/common/engram.py vllm/model_executor/model_loader/weight_utils.py
pre-commit run --files vllm/models/deepseek_v41/common/engram.py vllm/model_executor/model_loader/weight_utils.py
```

## Test Result

- Before: mypy reports the 3 `attr-defined` errors above.
- After: `Success: no issues found in 2 source files`. All other pre-commit
  hooks pass.

There is no behavior change on Linux, so model evaluation is not applicable.

## AI assistance

This change was prepared with AI assistance. A human submitter reviewed every
changed line and ran the commands above.

commits.pr_title: [CPU] Optimize routed INT8 W8A8 MoE GEMM dispatch
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Extend the routed CPU MoE dispatch approach from [#50949](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50949) to INT8 W8A8: select brgemm from each expert tile's actual row count instead of the call-wide average. Use brgemm for four-row tiles and share the existing tinygemm arithmetic between BF16 and FP16.

On a 32-core Qwen3 W8A8 serving comparison, the change improves the geometric mean of output throughput across nine concurrency levels by 1.41%, with 5.76% at concurrency 32 and 4.42% at concurrency 64. Peak-concurrency throughput remains at parity. The concurrency-32 baseline varies between repeats; both runs are shown below.

As #50949 describes the approach:
> Select BRGEMM from each expert block's actual `M` and `N`.

Open-PR searches for CPU INT8 MoE and routed GEMM dispatch found no duplicate. #50949 covers FP8/MXFP4; this change covers the separate INT8 W8A8 implementation.

## Claims

- Concentrated routing can use brgemm even when the average tokens per expert would select tinygemm.
- Both routed INT8 GEMM stages select their kernel per tile and release brgemm state when used by the parallel callback.
- BF16 and FP16 support small expert tiles through the same VNNI arithmetic, with conversion directly to the requested intermediate dtype.

## Validation

Reviewed head: `cedc8f26c0`; branch base: `9f3d70e081`.

```bash
# Focused checks: 68 passed during PR readiness review
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_cpu_quant_fused_moe.py \
  -k 'int8_w8a8 or small_expert_blocks' \
  tests/kernels/test_awq_int4_to_int8.py::TestInt4ScaledMmCpu -q

pre-commit run --files csrc/cpu/sgl-kernels/gemm.h \
  csrc/cpu/sgl-kernels/moe_int8.cpp \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_cpu_quant_fused_moe.py
git diff --check 9f3d70e081 HEAD
```

All applicable hooks passed. The BF16/FP16 test covers expert occupancies `(3, 4, 5, 33)`, including mixed dispatch and a block tail, and runs in CPU kernel CI. Commands omit host-specific affinity settings.

### Serving comparison

Following #50949's Sonnet 256/256 concurrency sweep, compare the same base and candidate with `RedHatAI/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507-quantized.w8a8` (revision `b2b37fb1c4cd5a5769b841ef1f672627b8304d8e`), BF16, TP=1, DP=1, and 32 physical compute cores.

| Concurrency | Base output tok/s (runs 1 / 2) | Candidate output tok/s (runs 1 / 2) | Mean throughput change |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 35.19 / 35.21 | 35.14 / 35.07 | -0.26% |
| 2 | 53.20 / 53.16 | 53.07 / 53.18 | -0.09% |
| 4 | 82.35 / 82.31 | 82.57 / 82.45 | +0.22% |
| 8 | 130.33 / 130.31 | 131.64 / 131.43 | +0.93% |
| 16 | 192.93 / 191.13 | 195.61 / 195.89 | +1.94% |
| 32 | 294.42 / 279.66 | 303.41 / 303.74 | +5.76% |
| 64 | 437.61 / 435.76 | 456.60 / 455.33 | +4.42% |
| 128 | 654.13 / 654.97 | 652.40 / 655.86 | -0.06% |
| 256 | 872.06 / 871.38 | 872.51 / 871.71 | +0.04% |

## Details

The previous selector uses `max(1, M * topk / E)` for the whole call. That average hides concentrated routing and expert-block tails. Both stages now use actual tile dimensions, skip empty tiles, and track brgemm use within each parallel callback.

The routed INT8 two-argument selector uses `M > 3` for full-width tiles. The existing one-argument selector continues to serve INT8 linear, INT4, and shared-expert callers. FP8/MXFP4 thresholds are unchanged.

AI assistance was used for implementation, review, and this description.

commits.pr_title: [XPU] [Feature] Adding triton/sycl GDN toggle
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Adds a `sycl` choice to `--gdn-prefill-backend` so the GDN attention kernel can be selected on XPU.

On XPU, `QwenGatedDeltaNetAttention` previously always called the fused SYCL op `_xpu_C::gdn_attention`, with no way to switch to the Triton/FLA kernels. This PR:

- Adds `sycl` to `--gdn-prefill-backend` (XPU only). Unlike the other choices, it selects a fused whole-layer op, so conv1d and decode are replaced as well as prefill.
- Keeps `forward_xpu` for the Qwen GDN layer and dispatches inside it: `gdn_attention_core_xpu` for SYCL, `qwen_gdn_attention_core` for Triton.
- Resolves `sycl` in `_resolve_gdn_prefill_backend`; the function signature is unchanged. With `auto`, Qwen gets SYCL whenever `_xpu_C::gdn_attention` is built, which matches the previous default behavior. `auto` never fails; without the kernel it uses Triton/FLA.
- OLMo Hybrid rejects `sycl` explicitly. Its layer calls the FLA kernels directly and cannot use the SYCL op: the op hardcodes `beta = sigmoid(b)`, which does not cover `linear_allow_neg_eigval`. `GDNAttentionMetadataBuilder` treats `sycl` like Triton and builds the FLA chunk metadata.
- Requesting `sycl` when it cannot be honored raises `ValueError` at startup instead of silently running a different kernel: on a non-XPU platform, when `_xpu_C::gdn_attention` is not built, or for OLMo Hybrid.

Behavior on XPU:

| Model | no flag (`auto`) | `triton` | `sycl` |
|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.5 / Qwen3-Next | SYCL (Triton/FLA if kernel not built) | Triton/FLA | SYCL (`ValueError` if kernel not built) |
| OLMo Hybrid | Triton/FLA | Triton/FLA | `ValueError` at startup |

CUDA/ROCm/CPU behavior is unchanged for existing choices; `sycl` raises `ValueError` there.

Not a duplicate: searching open PRs for `gdn sycl` returns only this PR and #50038, which is unrelated (FlashAttention-in-graph gating on oneAPI 2026.0+).

AI assistance was used for parts of this change. All changed lines were reviewed and tested by the submitter.

## Test Plan

Intel Arc Pro B60 (1 GPU per run), image `vllm/vllm-openai-xpu:latest` with the PR source (`2ecc4d62a9`) on `PYTHONPATH`, torch `2.14.0+xpu`. All runs are sequential, one run per configuration. Full logs with the exact command at the top of each are attached.

Qwen3.5-4B throughput (real weights):

```
vllm bench throughput --model Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B [--gdn-prefill-backend {triton,sycl}] \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 128 \
  --num-prompts 8 --max-num-seqs 64 --kv-cache-memory-bytes 6785272525 \
  --dtype bfloat16 --max-model-len 4096 --no-enable-prefix-caching --seed 42
```

OLMo Hybrid 7B throughput (`--load-format dummy`: checks kernel selection and throughput, not output quality):

```
vllm bench throughput --model allenai/Olmo-Hybrid-7B --load-format dummy \
  [--gdn-prefill-backend {triton,sycl}] --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len 512 --random-output-len 64 --num-prompts 4 --max-num-seqs 8 \
  --kv-cache-memory-bytes 2147483648 --dtype bfloat16 --max-model-len 2048 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching --seed 42
```

Accuracy, gsm8k 5-shot on Qwen3.5-4B, Triton/FLA vs SYCL (lm_eval `0.4.12`):

```
lm_eval run --model vllm --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --batch_size auto \
  --model_args pretrained=Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B dtype=bfloat16 seed=42 max_model_len=4096 \
  kv_cache_memory_bytes=6785272525 gdn_prefill_backend={triton,sycl}
```

Lint: `pre-commit run --files <changed files>` and `pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual --files <changed files>`.

## Test Result

`_log_gdn_backend_decision` does not log on XPU (#54871), so the kernel column is based on the requested backend in `non-default args` and the warmup time: Triton/FLA spends 267–325 s autotuning during the initial profiling run, while SYCL takes 0.06–0.07 s.

Qwen3.5-4B:

| Flag | Kernel | req/s | total tok/s | output tok/s | Initial profiling run | Engine init |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| none | SYCL | 1.90 | 2185.87 | 242.87 | 0.07 s | 58.4 s |
| `triton` | Triton/FLA | 1.53 | 1765.35 | 196.15 | 267.09 s | 331.7 s |
| `sycl` | SYCL | 1.91 | 2205.63 | 245.07 | 0.07 s | 60.3 s |

SYCL gives about 25% higher total throughput than Triton/FLA (one run per configuration). Engine init is about 4.5 min shorter with SYCL because Triton/FLA autotunes its kernels during the initial profiling run.

OLMo Hybrid 7B (dummy weights):

| Flag | Kernel | req/s | total tok/s | output tok/s |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| none | Triton/FLA | 1.07 | 614.60 | 68.29 |
| `triton` | Triton/FLA | 1.02 | 587.47 | 65.27 |
| `sycl` | – | `ValueError: GDN prefill backend 'sycl' is not supported for OLMo Hybrid.` at startup | – | – |

Both OLMo runs use the same kernel, so the throughput difference is run-to-run variation.

gsm8k (5-shot, 1319 samples), Qwen3.5-4B:

| Backend | exact_match, flexible-extract | exact_match, strict-match |
|---|---|---|
| `triton` | 0.7536 ± 0.0119 | 0.7384 ± 0.0121 |
| `sycl` | 0.7528 ± 0.0119 | 0.7384 ± 0.0121 |

Strict-match is identical; flexible-extract differs by one sample, well within the standard error. SYCL does not change accuracy.

Lint: all hooks pass, including mypy 3.10 and mypy 3.12.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Compile] Fuse AITER static FP8 quant into MLA attention output
commits.pr_body:
Fuse MLA attention with AITER's static per-tensor FP8 output quant on ROCm. Closes #62339.

- With AITER on and `fuse_attn_quant` enabled, MLA output quant now fuses into the attention op. On DeepSeek-Coder-V2-Lite-Instruct-FP8, 27 of 27 layers match (0 before).
- The fused path runs AITER's quant straight into the FP8 output, so it uses the same kernel as the unfused graph. Numerics are unchanged, and performance is neutral.
- No change on CUDA, or on ROCm with AITER off.

Specifically:
- `RocmMLAAttnFp8StaticQuantPattern` mirrors `RocmAttnFp8StaticQuantPattern` from #58099. AITER's per-tensor quant declares `scale` mutable, so the pattern returns it and the replacement passes it through. It is registered only on ROCm with AITER enabled.
- Matching alone made decode 2.4% slower at batch 4 (2.476 vs 2.417 s, ranges not overlapping). The fused MLA path computed bf16 output, then ran `QuantFP8` and a `copy_`, which replaced the graph's single AITER quant kernel. Running AITER's quant directly into the output removes that cost. It is gated on whether `QuantFP8` itself dispatches to AITER, so fused and unfused always use the same quant and clamp.
- This is parity rather than a speedup. On ROCm the MLA decode output is still produced in bf16 by the v_up_proj BMM and quantized afterwards. A real gain needs that BMM to write FP8 directly.
- No open PR covers this: searched for #62339, `MLAAttnQuantFusionPass` and MLA + AITER quant fusion.

Validated on: MI300X, AITER v0.1.25, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`, RedHatAI/DeepSeek-Coder-V2-Lite-Instruct-FP8 (static FP8, `ROCM_AITER_MLA`), `--compilation-config '{"pass_config":{"fuse_attn_quant":true}}'`. "Before" is this branch with the new pattern unregistered.

|---|---|---|---|
| `mla_attn_quant_fusion` matches | 0 | 27 | |
| `vllm bench latency` 32 in / 512 out, batch 4 (4 interleaved runs) | 2.454 s [2.426-2.482] | 2.443 s [2.409-2.483] | 0.996 |
| batch 32 | 3.950 s [3.906-3.996] | 3.958 s [3.892-3.966] | 1.002 |
| `vllm bench serve` random 1024/256, conc 4, TPOT p50 (3 runs) | 4.70 ms [4.68-4.75] | 4.59 ms [4.57-4.70] | 0.977 |
| conc 32, TPOT p50 | 7.79 ms [7.75-7.85] | 7.78 ms [7.68-7.82] | 0.999 |
| rate inf, output tok/s | 11724 [11722-11834] | 11791 [11740-11878] | 1.006 |
| gsm8k 5-shot flexible / strict | 0.767 / 0.755 | 0.765 / 0.752 | McNemar p = 0.86 / 0.80 |

Tests:
- `pytest tests/compile/passes/test_mla_attn_quant_fusion.py tests/compile/passes/test_fusion_attn.py` passes 10/10 (31 passed, 24 skipped).
- `test_mla_attn_quant_fusion.py` passes with `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER` unset, `=1` and `=0`.

commits.pr_title: [PCP] Allow decode-only full CUDA graphs for DSv3.2/GLM-5.2/5.3 sparse MLA with DCP=1
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Allows decode-only full CUDA graphs (`FULL_DECODE_ONLY` / `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`) under MRV2 PCP with DCP=1 for sparse-MLA models on the DeepSeek-V3.2 attention path (DeepSeek-V3.2 and GLM-5.2/5.3: `deepseek_v32`, `glm_moe_dsa`). In that mode, decode requests are round-robin sharded across PCP ranks. These models previously had to run with `cudagraph_mode=NONE`, but the pure-decode full-graph path from #53867 already handles them. Other `index_topk` models (DSv4/V4.1, MiniMax-M3, ...) still require `NONE`, because they need model-specific work (see #61555 for DSv4.1).

## Claims

- GLM-5.3 with TP1 × PCP4 + EP captures and replays decode-only full CUDA graphs.
- On GSM8K, that is 2.6× faster than eager, with matching accuracy (0.9083 vs 0.9075).

## Validation

Tested with GLM-5.3-NVFP4 on 4×B300: `-tp 1 -pcp 4 --enable-expert-parallel --kv-cache-dtype fp8`, `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`, `tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --num-questions 1319 --max-concurrency 64`:

| cudagraph_mode | GSM8K accuracy | Wall time | Output tok/s |
|---|---|---|---|
| NONE | 0.9075 | 379.5 s | 330 |
| FULL_AND_PIECEWISE | 0.9083 | 145.9 s | 859 |

Every rank captured 11 FULL and 19 PIECEWISE graphs.

`pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_pcp_manager.py`: passes.

## Details

- Pure FULL mode is still rejected, so prefills under PCP keep running piecewise.
- DeepSeek-V3.2 shares GLM-5.3's attention/indexer code but was not run end-to-end.
- Not validated yet with MTP.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Core] Requeue encoder-stalled waiting requests
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

A waiting request can end a scheduling pass with `num_new_tokens == 0`: its encoder inputs do not fit the cache or the compute budget, or the prefill-lookahead reserve consumes the tokens. The waiting loop `break`ed there, so the request kept its head-of-queue position and every request behind it went unscheduled for that step — repeating on every step while the resource condition holds.

It is now requeued with `skip_request()`, which preserves the drain-first priority of requests holding KV blocks (async KV-load resumes) and the `deferred_waiting` accounting.

The self-pinned encoder-cache release from the earlier revision is dropped here; #60553 proposes that.

### Duplicate-work check

Searched open issues and PRs for waiting-queue requeue / head-of-line blocking and encoder cache stalls. No open PR touches this path; the nearest matches are #56826 and #57368 (encoder input lifetimes across steps — different concern), #40707/#40709 (mamba split deadlock — different path), and umbrella EPD tracker #52409.

## Test Plan

```bash
ruff format --check vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py
ruff check vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py tests/v1/core/test_encoder_cache_manager.py tests/v1/core/test_async_scheduler.py -q
```

## Test Result

- `ruff format --check` and `ruff check` clean.
- 248 passed, 1 failed. The failure is `test_encoder_cache_embed_count_mismatch_restores_prior_hit_state`: the mismatch path also returns zero tokens, so the `encoder_cache_manager.free(request)` added in d12809f1 drops the prior-hit references that test guards. It fails at 5219f995 as well, so it is not introduced by this drop.
- 3 tests in `tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py` cover the requeue: queue head-of-line starvation, `deferred_waiting` accounting, drain-first queue membership.
- No model eval: the change only alters failure-path control flow, no logits-affecting code.

## AI Assistance

AI assistance was used (pi coding agent): analysis, draft and test runs. The human author reviewed every changed line, ran the checks above, and defends the change end-to-end.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][DSv4.1] Keep the Engram all-to-all buffers in one allocator
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

DeepSeek-V4.1 with host-offloaded, DP-sharded Engram tables (`cpu_offload: true`, `dp_shared_memory: false`, e.g. with `use_thp: true`) hangs in the first forward (memory profiling) when `--enable-cumem-allocator` is set. This receives the Engram all-to-all into a persistent buffer allocated next to its send buffer, so both come from the same allocator.

No open PR covers this (searched open PRs/issues for Engram all-to-all, cumem, `NCCL_LOCAL_REGISTER`). #62091 changes only the GPU-table path (`cpu_offload: false`), which has no all-to-all.

## Claims

- Fixes the hang: DSv4.1-Flash DEP2/DEP4 prefill with host DP-sharded Engram + `--enable-cumem-allocator` now starts and serves.
- No numerical change: the same bytes are exchanged, only the receive buffer's allocation changes. Peak memory is unchanged (the per-step `empty_like` of the same size becomes persistent).

## Validation

GB200 (4 GPUs/node), vLLM nightly 49cb2bbf image (CUDA 13.4, NCCL 2.32.3), env `NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE=1 NCCL_MNNVL_ENABLE=1 NCCL_NVLS_ENABLE=1`. The changed code is identical on main.

Serving: `vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --data-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel --enable-cumem-allocator --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true,"embedding_across_dp":true,"use_thp":true}' --max-num-batched-tokens 32768 --kernel-config '{"moe_backend":"deep_gemm_mega_moe"}' ...` (same hang with DEP2).

| run | result |
|---|---|
| main | hangs in `determine_available_memory`; all ranks in `EngramBatch._stage` `all_to_all_single` (py-spy, also with `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1`), GPUs spin at 100%, NCCL watchdog fires after 600 s |
| main, no `--enable-cumem-allocator` | starts |
| main, `NCCL_LOCAL_REGISTER=0` | starts |
| this PR | starts (profiling + CUDA graph capture); 48/48 completions with 8 to 30K-word prompts at concurrency 16 (both the all-to-all and the peer-exchange slots) |

Standalone reproducer, no model (4 GPUs):

<details>
<summary>repro.py</summary>

```python
# torchrun --nproc-per-node 4 repro.py [--same-pool]
import os
import sys

import torch
import torch.distributed as dist

from vllm.device_allocator.cumem import CuMemAllocator

torch.cuda.set_device(int(os.environ["LOCAL_RANK"]))
dist.init_process_group("nccl")
shape = (32768 * dist.get_world_size(), 2, 6, 264)
with CuMemAllocator.get_instance().use_memory_pool(tag="weights"):
    sent = torch.zeros(shape, dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda")
    pool_recv = torch.zeros(shape, dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda")
recv = pool_recv if "--same-pool" in sys.argv else torch.zeros_like(sent)
dist.all_to_all_single(recv, sent)
torch.cuda.synchronize()
print(f"rank {dist.get_rank()} ok")
```

</details>

| send | recv | result |
|---|---|---|
| cumem pool | caching allocator | hangs (killed after 120 s) |
| cumem pool | cumem pool (`--same-pool`) | ok |
| cumem pool | caching allocator, `NCCL_LOCAL_REGISTER=0` | ok |

`pre-commit run --files vllm/models/deepseek_v41/common/engram.py` passes. No test added: reproducing needs 4+ GPUs with NCCL 2.32 and the cumem allocator, which CI does not run for DSv4.1; validation above was done outside CI.

## Details

Root cause: `EngramBatch.__init__` runs during model init, inside the cumem pool when `--enable-cumem-allocator` is set, so `packed_rows` (the all-to-all send buffer) is a cumem allocation. The receive buffer was `torch.empty_like(rows)` in each forward, from the caching allocator. With NCCL local user-buffer registration on (the default), NCCL 2.32 hangs an all-to-all whose buffers mix the two allocators; the reproducer shows this without the model. I did not pin down the NCCL-internal reason (the serving logs show FABRIC IPC registration failures for some buffers, the reproducer hangs without them).

Allocating the receive buffer next to `packed_rows` keeps both in one allocator in either mode, and removes a per-step allocation. `_stage` is an eager break, so the persistent buffer does not affect CUDA graphs.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to investigate and write this change; I reviewed every line and ran the validation above.

commits.pr_title: [Frontend] Serve Gemma 4 on /v1/systemone and /v1/decisions
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Serve the Gemma 4 family on `/v1/systemone` and `/v1/decisions` by mapping its architectures to the existing `NextTokenStrategy`. This addresses #62096 with the alternative the issue suggests, adding Gemma 4 to the supported list. A default for every generation model is left to RFC #59365.

```bash
vllm serve google/gemma-4-12B-it
```

## Claims

- `Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration` (E2B, E4B, 26B-A4B, 31B), `Gemma4UnifiedForConditionalGeneration` (12B) and `Gemma4ForCausalLM` (text-only exports) now serve both endpoints. Before this change, both returned 501.
- With thinking off, each Gemma 4 chat template ends where the label is the reply's first token. All 38 labels (A–Z, yes/no, 0–9) are one token there. A CPU test pins both template variants.
- Other generation models stay unsupported. This widens the allowlist and adds no default.

## Validation

**Templates and labels (CPU).** `test_gemma4_labels_start_the_reply` builds `NextTokenStrategy` from the `google/gemma-4-E2B-it` and `google/gemma-4-12B-it` tokenizers. Construction fails unless every label is one distinct token at the start of the reply. The E2B/E4B prompt ends at `<|turn>model\n`. The 12B/26B/31B prompt ends with a closed empty thought, `<|turn>model\n<|channel>thought\n<channel|>`.

**End to end.** I ran main at `3c13653738` with this patch, installed with `VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1`. Each model ran the existing `/v1/systemone` e2e suite (`test_structured_decisions_e2e.py`) with `MODEL_NAME` swapped and `--max-model-len 4096`. Each model also answered the first 200 AG News test rows as a 4-way `choice`, with the article as the state; that sample has about ±6% error at 95%. Before the patch, `vllm serve google/gemma-4-E2B-it` returns 501 on both endpoints.

| Model | Served as | GPU, weights | e2e suite | AG News acc. | mean `label_mass` | `argmax_is_label` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `google/gemma-4-E2B-it` | `Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration` | L4, bf16 | 13/13 | 0.790 | 0.729 | 0.775 |
| `google/gemma-4-E2B-it` | `Gemma4ForCausalLM` (via `--hf-overrides`) | L4, bf16 | 13/13 | 0.790 | 0.728 | 0.770 |
| `google/gemma-4-E4B-it` | `Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration` | A100, bf16 | 13/13 | 0.830 | 1.000 | 1.000 |
| `google/gemma-4-12B-it` | `Gemma4UnifiedForConditionalGeneration` | A100, bf16 | 13/13 | 0.865 | 0.990 | 0.990 |
| `google/gemma-4-12B-it` | `Gemma4UnifiedForConditionalGeneration` | L4, fp8 | 13/13 | 0.860 | 0.991 | 0.995 |
| `google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it` | `Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration` | A100, fp8 | 13/13 | 0.815 | 0.985 | 0.985 |
| `google/gemma-4-31B-it` | `Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration` | A100, fp8 | 13/13 | 0.865 | 1.000 | 1.000 |
| `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B` (already supported) | `Qwen3ForCausalLM` | L4, bf16 | 13/13 | 0.795 | 0.638 | 0.730 |

The A100 was the 40 GB model, so 26B-A4B and 31B ran with `--quantization fp8`. `/v1/decisions` returned 200 for the docs example on every run.

**Tests.**

```bash
pytest tests/entrypoints/generate/structured_decisions/test_strategies.py
# 55 passed (macOS CPU and L4)
pytest tests/entrypoints/generate/structured_decisions/test_decisions.py tests/entrypoints/generate/structured_decisions/test_question_types.py
# 49 passed
```

Without the `strategies.py` change, `test_strategy_selection` fails with "does not support Gemma4ForCausalLM". A template that leaves `<|channel>thought\n` open still constructs `NextTokenStrategy`, so the test's prompt-ending assertion is what catches that.

**Not covered in CI.** No Gemma 4 checkpoint runs in CI, as in #60676 and #61064. The CPU test downloads two Gemma 4 tokenizers (31 MB each).

## Details

- **Why not a default for every generation model.** Review on #59299 asked that models opt in once their read is known to work, after a DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash read came back wrong. At startup the server only checks that each label is one token after the generation prompt. It cannot tell whether the reply starts with the answer, so a template that opens a thought or a channel returns 200 with noise. RFC #59365 proposes a next-token fallback behind a strategy registry, and this PR leaves that open.
- **Why no new strategy.** Each checkpoint's own template already ends where the answer starts, and it should not be swapped. Serving E2B with the 12B template, whose only difference is the empty thought, drops `argmax_is_label` from 0.77 to 0.00 and AG News accuracy from 0.79 to 0.30.
- **E2B.** Its misses are a preamble, not a thought: in 45 of the 46 non-label reads the top token is `The`. `label_mass` reports this. E4B uses the same template and lands every read on a label.
- **`Gemma4ForCausalLM`.** No Google checkpoint declares it, but text-only exports do. For example, `LilaRest/gemma-4-31B-it-NVFP4-turbo` has 147k downloads, and its template also closes an empty thought. I also checked this architecture by serving E2B with `--hf-overrides '{"architectures": ["Gemma4ForCausalLM"]}'`.
- **Startup.** A Gemma 4 checkpoint without a chat template, such as the base `google/gemma-4-E2B`, fails `NextTokenStrategy` with a `ValueError`. The server still starts, and both endpoints return 501 as before.
- **Speculative decoding.** With MTP, `logprob_token_ids` reads can return 500 when they share a batch with draft requests, until #42592 is fixed (#44727 and #61219 are open). This affects every next-token model, and Gemma 4 is often served with MTP.
- **Media.** `NextTokenStrategy` takes no media yet, so Gemma 4 reads are text-only until #62181.
- **Not a duplicate.** No open PR adds Gemma 4 to `NextTokenStrategy`. I searched for 62096 and for keywords such as `READ_STRATEGIES`, `NextTokenStrategy`, systemone, decisions and gemma. Related PRs:
  - #60713 (Winnow) picks its own strategy from an explicit `decision_read_strategy` override before this lookup, so it still works. Its test asserts that a plain `Gemma4ForCausalLM` is unsupported, so whichever PR lands second updates that line.
  - #61251's splice test would need Gemma 4 entries in `SPLICE_MODELS`.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][LoRA] Apply text-only LoRAs to the LM of multimodal wrappers
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fixes #48019. A LoRA trained on the text-only `*ForCausalLM` of a multimodal model silently does nothing when served on the multimodal wrapper. This resolves such adapters on the model side, in `LoRAModelManager._get_lora_layer_weights`, so it works for every multimodal wrapper without per-model mapper rules.

This builds on #49525 by @fooSynaptic (co-author), which fixes the same bug through a `WeightsMapper` fallback and only covers wrappers whose mapper has a `model.language_model.` rule. This PR covers those wrappers too, plus the ones without such a rule.

## Claims

- Text-named adapters (`model.layers.*` / `lm_head`) now apply to the language model of multimodal wrappers, including wrappers with no `model.language_model.` mapper rule or a different LM prefix (`llm.`, `model.text_model.`), e.g. Llama4, DeepSeek-V4, MiniCPM-V, Idefics3/SmolVLM.
- Adapters that already match (trained on the full multimodal class), tower/connector LoRA, and text-only models are unchanged.

## Validation

```bash
pytest tests/lora/test_lora_manager.py tests/lora/test_utils.py tests/lora/test_lora_checkpoints.py
```

- New test `test_text_only_lora_binds_to_multimodal_language_model`: 3 passed (all 3 fail on main).
- The three files above: 58 passed.

E2E on 1x H20: one synthetic r=16 LoRA on the LM's q/k/v/o/gate/up/down_proj, saved twice: text-named (`base_model.model.model.layers.*`) and wrapper-named (`base_model.model.model.language_model.layers.*`, or `model.text_model.layers.*` for SmolVLM). Prompt logprobs of 4 prompts from vLLM base / text-named / wrapper-named, compared with an HF reference that has the LoRA merged into the weights.

Mean |Δ logprob| of the text-named adapter vs vLLM base (HF LoRA effect in parentheses):

| model | main | #49525 | this PR | this PR vs HF LoRA (wrapper-named vs HF) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.5-4B-Base (0.056) | 0.0000 | 0.0534 | 0.0535 | 0.0146 (0.0134) |
| llava-1.5-7b-hf (0.060) | 0.0000 | 0.0575 | 0.0565 | 0.0126 (0.0111) |
| SmolVLM-256M-Instruct (0.104) | 0.0000 | **0.0000** | 0.0948 | 0.0486 (0.0507) |

vLLM-vs-HF base noise: 0.017 / 0.017 / 0.063. Llama4 and DeepSeek-V4 were not run (too large); they use the same `language_model.` prefix path as Qwen3.5.

## Details

**Root cause.** PEFT on the text-only class (what `AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained("Qwen/Qwen3.5-*")` returns in transformers 5.x, i.e. the default TRL SFT path) names modules `model.layers.*` / `lm_head`. vLLM's multimodal wrappers mount the language model under `language_model.`, `llm.` or `model.text_model.`. `activate_adapter` looks weights up by the full module name, finds none, and serves the base model; load-time validation only checks the leaf name (`q_proj`), so nothing fails.

**Fix.** When a LoRA module has no exact match and lives under `get_mm_mapping().language_model`, look it up by its text-only name: the remainder after the prefix, or the remainder under `model.` when the prefix holds a bare decoder. All lookups, including packed (`qkv_proj`, `gate_up_proj`) and MoE packing, go through this function; text-named entries consumed by packing are dropped like the other sub-module entries.

- Exact names always win, so adapters trained on the full multimodal class are unaffected. No tower/connector prefix of any in-tree LoRA-capable multimodal model is nested under its LM prefix, so tower/connector lookups are unchanged.
- The lookup is driven by the model's real modules, so there is no double-mapping risk (e.g. `model.language_model. -> model.` mappers) and no effect on layers owned by other PP ranks.
- No change to base-weight loading or to any model's `hf_to_vllm_mapper`.
- No new validation or error path, and no separate name-matching logic: the fallback lives inside the existing lookup, so any future "adapter matches nothing" check can reuse `_get_lora_layer_weights` and stay consistent with what is actually applied.

commits.pr_title: [Model] Add ColUltraVBERT late-interaction retrieval model
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Adds `ColUltraVBertForRetrieval` for [athrael-soju/ColUltraVBERT](https://huggingface.co/athrael-soju/ColUltraVBERT),
a 255M-parameter late-interaction retriever for visual documents. vLLM loads the checkpoint's Sentence Transformers
package and returns L2-normalized 768-d token vectors through `token_embed`, scored by MaxSim.

## Claims

- vLLM serves `ColUltraVBertForRetrieval` for text and page images with `runner="pooling"`.
- ViDoRe nDCG@5 matches the reference within 0.001.

## Validation

```bash
pytest tests/models/multimodal/pooling/test_colultravbert.py tests/models/test_registry.py
pytest "tests/models/test_initialization.py::test_can_initialize_large_subset[ColUltraVBertForRetrieval]"
```

All pass: the 11 ColUltraVBERT tests (7 tile-cap cases against grids from the checkpoint's image
processor), the registry (409 passed, 11 skipped) and the initialization test.

Parity against the checkpoint's Sentence Transformers `MultiVectorEncoder` on 32 ViDoRe pages and 32 queries, with
identical token ids:

| dtype | Pages, mean cosine (min item) | Queries, mean cosine (min item) | MaxSim top-1 agreement |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| fp32 | 0.99987 (0.9987) | 0.99987 (0.9961) | 100% |
| bf16 | 0.9971 (0.9955) | 0.9966 (0.9561) | 100% |

The lowest tokens are tile separators and query padding tokens, which also move between the reference's own fp32 runs.

ViDoRe nDCG@5 (bf16), same harness:

| Task | Reference | vLLM |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| DocVQA | 0.5263 | 0.5257 |
| TabFQuAD | 0.9251 | 0.9257 |

## Details

Follows `colmodernvbert.py`, with these differences:

- UltraBERT text encoder: RMSNorm and SwiGLU layers alternating sliding-window and full attention, each with its own
  RoPE base. UltraBERT's `sliding_window` is an inclusive radius, so vLLM gets `sliding_window + 1`.
- RMSNorm after the connector's projection.
- Pages tile through vLLM's Idefics3 processing at a 3,072 px longest edge, capped at 27 tiles of 512 px plus a global
  view; the cap lowers the longest edge per image in 512 px steps, as the checkpoint's image processor does.
- The pooler applies the package's `1_Dense` projection.
- `ColUltraVBertConfig` is vendored, because UltraBERT needs transformers 5.20 and vLLM pins below it.

Pages use the prompt `User:<image>Describe the image.<end_of_utterance>\nAssistant:`; queries append ten
`<end_of_utterance>` tokens. The docs include an `LLM.encode` example.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Benchmark] Don't count content-free chunks as streamed outputs in chat
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

The chat benchmark clients count the opening role-only chunk as a streamed output, so TTFT is measured to a chunk with no output in it and the first real token appends a spurious ITL sample. A check prevented this between #3768 and #12288; this restores it in a form that also handles `reasoning` and `tool_calls`. Original report: #3759.

Benchmark client only. No engine, scheduler or serving code is touched, and no measured figure here reflects a change in how fast vLLM runs.

## Claims

- TTFT for `--backend openai-chat` is measured to the opening `delta: {"role": "assistant", "content": ""}` chunk, which carries no output.
- As a result 208 of 600 requests recorded `len(itl) == output_tokens`, which cannot happen when every interval sits between two tokens; there are at most `output_tokens - 1`. `/v1/completions` on the same server recorded exactly 200 x 255 samples and zero impossible counts.
- Every request on `main` carried a first ITL sample timing the role chunk, median 4 microseconds, so the minimum and low percentiles time metadata arrival. The error runs in the flattering direction: `main` reports chat as slightly faster than it is. With the fix, the minimum and each request's first sample rise to real decode intervals, and vLLM's actual speed is unchanged.
- This does **not** materially change any printed summary metric. Mean and median TTFT, ITL and TPOT all move by less than the run-to-run spread. The fix is to the sample array, which `--save-detailed` writes to JSON.
- 43 lines across the two clients, no new abstraction, no change to `async_request_openai_completions` or `async_request_openai_audio`.

## Validation

Four behaviours added to `tests/benchmarks/test_endpoint_request_func_timing.py`, parametrized over the packaged and legacy clients. 18 tests to 26, all passing. All eight fail against current `main`:

| behaviour | fails on `main` as |
|---|---|
| opening role chunk is not a streamed output | `assert 5 == (5 - 1)` on the interval count |
| mid-stream content-free chunk adds no interval | `assert 4 == (3 - 1)` |
| stream with no streamed output is rejected | `assert not output.success`; `main` marks it successful |
| token rendering as an empty string is counted | `assert len(output.itl) == 2`, got 3, TTFT on the role chunk |

```
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/benchmarks/test_endpoint_request_func_timing.py -v
```

`pre-commit run --files` clean on all three files. The test file gains 188 lines and loses 2: two small chunk builders, `_role_chunk` and `_empty_chunk`, the four tests, and the module docstring reworded to describe them. The two removed lines are the old docstring wording. No existing test function is modified and no other test file is touched.

End-to-end on one RTX 3080, `Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B`, three interleaved blocks per side against a single server, 200 requests each, 600 per side, 256 output tokens, concurrency 64:

```
vllm bench serve --model Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B --port 8031 --backend openai-chat \
  --endpoint /v1/chat/completions --dataset-name random --num-prompts 200 \
  --output-len 256 --max-concurrency 64 --save-result --save-detailed
```

Across those 600 requests on `main`:

- all 600 had a first sample under 0.1 ms, timing the arrival of the role chunk, median 0.0040 ms. That is exactly one spurious sample per request and never more than one, and it is what drags the reported minimum ITL down to 0.0025 ms.
- 208 recorded `len(itl) == output_tokens`, more intervals than exist between that many tokens. These are the requests where no two tokens happened to share a read, so nothing offset the extra sample. The other 392 carried it too and landed under the limit.

On this branch, no request records `len(itl) == output_tokens` and none exceeds `output_tokens - 1`. Two of 600 had a first sample under 0.1 ms, both from two tokens arriving in a single read.

Total sample counts are not compared here. They differ between separate runs against a live server because the server coalesces tokens differently each time, so a gap between two runs' totals is not evidence of anything.

`/v1/completions` on the same server, same workload, recorded exactly 51,000 samples for 200 requests of 256 tokens, which is 200 x 255, and no impossible counts.

<details>
<summary>Printed summary metrics, which do not meaningfully change</summary>

Pooled over the three blocks per side, with the spread across `main`'s own three blocks for comparison:

| metric | main | this branch | delta | main's block spread |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Mean TTFT | 463.74 ms | 251.13 ms | -212.61 | 724.23 |
| Median TTFT | 332.08 ms | 232.07 ms | -100.01 | 442.91 |
| P99 TTFT | 2465.88 ms | 423.67 ms | -2042.21 | 2293.71 |
| Mean ITL | 8.99 ms | 6.11 ms | -2.88 | 8.71 |
| Median ITL | 4.81 ms | 4.73 ms | -0.07 | 0.08 |
| P99 ITL | 114.96 ms | 53.65 ms | -61.32 | 71.91 |
| Mean TPOT | 8.94 ms | 5.98 ms | -2.96 | 8.79 |

Every delta is smaller than the spread between `main`'s own blocks, so none of it is a real difference; the pooled TTFT gap is mostly `main`'s first block being a cold start. The role chunk and the first token arrive about 4 microseconds apart, against swings of 85 ms in Mean TTFT between `main`'s two warm blocks alone.

The GPU also drives a display and was not idle during these runs. That is why the comparison is interleaved and why the spread column is included.

</details>

## Details

### Root cause

#3759 reported a chat TTFT of 0.005 s and printed the chunk it had been measured to, a role-only delta with `content: null`. @ywang96 identified the role chunk as the cause and #3768 added:

```python
delta = data["choices"][0]["delta"]
if delta.get("content", None):
```

#12288 restructured the same block to read token counts from the usage chunk. That required tolerating a trailing chunk with `choices: []`, since `data["choices"][0]` raises on it, and the gate became:

```python
if choices := data.get("choices"):
    content = choices[0]["delta"].get("content")
```

`content` is still read but no longer decides anything. The packaged client in `vllm/benchmarks/lib/` has the same shape. #3768's own note explains why nothing caught it: "This does not affect existing CI results since by default vLLM uses completions instead of chat completions for benchmarking."

### Tokens that render as empty strings

#12288 left this note on the completions side:

```python
if choices := data.get("choices"):
    # Note that text could be empty here
    # e.g. for special tokens
    text = choices[0].get("text")
```

That is correct: a token can decode to an empty string under `skip_special_tokens=True`, and dropping it would lose a real interval. #3768's truthiness gate would drop it. So the check here tests whether the chunk carries a token:

```python
if delta.get("content") or delta.get("reasoning") or delta.get("tool_calls") or delta.get("function_call"):
    return True
return delta.get("content") == "" and "role" not in delta
```

The two cases are distinguishable on the wire. An empty-rendering token serialises as `{"content": ""}`. The opening chunk serialises as `{"role": "assistant", "content": ""}`, and `role` is set only there, on the first iteration of `chat_completion_stream_generator`, and on no other `DeltaMessage` in the streaming path. A suppressed or finish chunk serialises as `{}`. A third-party server that repeats `role` on every chunk is unaffected, because a chunk with real content satisfies the first condition.

Three of the four fields, `content`, `reasoning` and `tool_calls`, are what vLLM's own streaming logger checks to decide whether a delta carried anything, in the same file. `function_call` is the fourth and vLLM never emits it; it is there because OpenAI's legacy spec puts it on streaming deltas and these clients are pointed at third-party OpenAI-compatible servers too.

### Tradeoffs and notes

The gate is a named helper with one call site per file, which §3.3 of the PR checklist would normally have inlined. It is kept because the two clients must stay in sync, per #55508, and a shared name makes a divergence between them visible; and because the second condition needs the comment explaining why an empty string counts, which reads badly inline.

Content-free chunks now reach the `elif usage:` branch, which the `if choices:` arm used to swallow. Under `continuous_usage_stats` the opening chunk carries both `choices` and `usage`, so its `completion_tokens: 0` is read and then overwritten by every later chunk. For servers that attach usage to an empty finish chunk with no trailing `choices: []` chunk, the count is now captured where it was dropped before.

`most_recent_timestamp` advances only inside the gated branch, so #55508's `latency - ttft == sum(itl)` guarantee is unchanged. #54708's rejection of tokenless streams is unchanged and now also fires on a stream whose chunks all carry content-free `choices`.

### Relation to #46652

#46652 proposed inserting zero-duration ITL samples so `len(itl)` matched the token count. `docs/benchmarking/cli.md` says ITL records only the gaps between streamed outputs and adds no zero-duration gaps for tokens in the same output, so #46652 is closed. This PR removes a sample with no output on either side of it. Both came out of #27485, which the stale bot closed; the reasoning and tool-parser case reported there is a different cause.

### Duplicate check

Nobody is fixing this. Every reference to #3759, #3768 and #12288 across issues and PRs is a coincidental numeric match; the 190 hits for 12288 are hidden and intermediate sizes. The regression was never re-reported after #12288 merged, so #3759 is still the only issue describing it.

A search by fix shape found nothing either. No PR restores a content gate, and `_choice_has_streamed_output` has no hits. #55508 touched this exact function on 2026-09-13 to make TTFT and latency accounting consistent across endpoints and left the gate ungated. #28183 attempted per-token ITL from continuous usage stats and was closed unmerged without adding a gate.

Open PRs touching either client file are #49720, #51155, #51172, #55719, #57519 and #58734. None modify the chunk gating. My own #46652 is in this area and is being closed.

#59722 is related. It reports the Rust `vllm-bench` chat backend counting token-less streams as successful and notes that Python fails them, which is true for the case tested there: a stream with no `choices` chunks at all, which `first_chunk_received` already rejects. It is not true for a stream whose chunks all carry content-free `choices`, which is the third behaviour above.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Reject LoRA at config time for models without SupportsLoRA
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Reject `enable_lora=True` during config validation for models that don't implement `SupportsLoRA`, instead of failing later inside EngineCore. Fixes #61850.

## Claims

- `LLM(model="Zyphra/Zamba2-7B-instruct", enable_lora=True)` now fails during config validation (a `ValidationError` from `VllmConfig`) with `LoRA is not supported for Zamba2ForCausalLM (Zyphra/Zamba2-7B-instruct). ...` instead of a bare `AssertionError` in EngineCore surfacing as `RuntimeError: Engine core initialization failed`.
- The check applies to every registered model without `SupportsLoRA` (125 architectures today), not only Zamba2 and Mamba2.
- No behavior change for models that support LoRA, or for any model run without `enable_lora`.

## Validation

Reproducer: the snippet from #61850, run on the CPU backend with `load_format="dummy"` (the failure happens in the model constructor, before weights load).

| Model | `enable_lora` | Before (main @ a97d19d792) | After |
|---|---|---|---|
| Zyphra/Zamba2-7B-instruct | True | `AssertionError` at `zamba2.py:719` → `Engine core initialization failed` | `ValidationError` at config validation, no EngineCore started |
| Zyphra/Zamba2-1.2B-instruct | False | starts and generates | starts and generates |
| yujiepan/mamba2-codestral-v0.1-tiny-random | True | `AssertionError` at `mamba2.py:106` → `Engine core initialization failed` | `ValidationError` at config validation |
| yujiepan/mamba2-codestral-v0.1-tiny-random | False | starts and generates | starts and generates |
| Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B | True | starts and generates | starts and generates |

<details>
<summary>Reproducer</summary>

```python
import sys
from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams

if __name__ == "__main__":
    model, lora = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2] == "lora"
    llm = LLM(model=model, enable_lora=lora, max_model_len=512, seed=42, load_format="dummy")
    print(llm.generate(["The capital of France is"], SamplingParams(temperature=0.0, max_tokens=8)))
```

</details>

Tests:

```bash
pytest tests/models/test_registry.py tests/test_config.py
```

- New tests: `test_registry_supports_lora` and `test_lora_rejected_at_config_time_for_unsupported_model`. They pass with this change; with the source changes reverted, the four cases that check the new behavior fail.
- Full `tests/models/test_registry.py` and `tests/test_config.py`: 838 passed vs. 833 on main, no new failures. The 14 failures that occur on both branches come from gated `meta-llama` checkpoints and CPU-environment limits.
- `ruff check` and `ruff format` pass.

Validated on the CPU backend only. The change touches config validation and the model registry, not device code; both test files run in CI (`models_basic.yaml`, `engine.yaml`).

## Details

**Root cause:** whether a model supports LoRA is already known from the `SupportsLoRA` interface, but it was only checked in `LoRAModelRunnerMixin.load_lora_model` (`lora_model_runner_mixin.py:47`), after the model is constructed inside the worker. `Zamba2Model` and `Mamba2Model` guard against LoRA with a bare `assert` in their constructors, which runs first, so the existing descriptive error was never reached, and the failure was only visible in EngineCore's stderr.

**Fix:** follows the existing pattern used for pipeline parallelism (`supports_pp` → `ModelConfig.is_pp_supported` → checked in `ModelConfig.verify_with_parallel_config`):

- `registry.py`: record `supports_lora` in `_ModelInfo`, computed with the existing `supports_lora()` helper.
- `config/model.py`: expose it as `ModelConfig.is_lora_supported`.
- `config/lora.py`: raise in `LoRAConfig.verify_with_model_config`, which already runs during `VllmConfig` validation.
- `zamba2.py`, `mamba2.py`: drop the now-unreachable asserts.

**Notes for reviewers:**

- No configuration that worked before is newly rejected: the runtime check calls the same `supports_lora()` on an instance of the same class, and no model sets `supports_lora` dynamically. Across all 390 loadable architectures, the class-level check also logs none of `supports_lora()`'s attribute-mismatch warnings.
- Cached model info from older versions lacks the new field; `_ModelInfo(**cached)` then raises, which `_load_modelinfo_from_cache` already catches, so the model is re-inspected.
- The runtime check in `LoRAModelRunnerMixin` is left in place.
- #61870 replaces the two asserts with `ValueError` in the constructors. That gives a clearer message, but it still runs inside EngineCore, so the user-facing error remains `Engine core initialization failed` (checked with the same reproducer). This PR moves the check to config validation, as the issue requests.

commits.pr_title: [Multimodal][Docs] State that retried media downloads count toward the request budget
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Make it visible that `VLLM_MAX_MEDIA_REQUEST_DOWNLOAD_SIZE_MB` counts retried download attempts. As discussed above with @jperezdealgaba and @DarkLight1337, counting them is intentional: it stops a media URL that keeps disconnecting from transferring several times the limit through retries. This PR keeps that behavior and says so in the error message and in `docs/usage/security.md`.

## Claims

- The budget error now reads `Request media downloads exceed VLLM_MAX_MEDIA_REQUEST_DOWNLOAD_SIZE_MB=… (N bytes received, including retried attempts).`, so an operator seeing it for media under the limit knows why.
- The `security.md` row now says the budget includes "concurrent downloads and retried attempts".
- New sync and async tests pin the restrictive behavior: a fetch that fails mid-body and is retried is charged for both attempts and raises with that message.
- No behavior change.

## Validation

```
$ pytest tests/test_connections.py
main:    2 failed, 7 passed  (new tests: message lacks "including retried attempts")
this PR: 9 passed
```

`pytest tests/test_connections.py tests/test_audio_media_size_precheck.py tests/multimodal/media -m "skip_global_cleanup or cpu_test"`: 110 passed, 3 failed. The 3 failures also happen on `main` in my environment: PyAV isn't installed.

`pre-commit run --hook-stage manual` on the changed files: all hooks pass (ruff, typos, markdownlint, mypy, test tethering, SPDX).

## Details

This PR originally refunded a failed attempt's bytes before the retry. That was rejected for the security reason above (see @jperezdealgaba's comment and the earlier thread on #61226), and the scope was changed to documenting the behavior, per @DarkLight1337. The branch history shows both commits; the final diff is one line in `vllm/connections.py`, one line in `docs/usage/security.md`, and tests.

The test helpers in `tests/test_connections.py` now accept an exception in the chunk list, to simulate a connection dropping mid-body.

**Duplicate check:** searched open/closed issues and PRs for `MediaRequestDownloadBudget` and `VLLM_MAX_MEDIA_REQUEST_DOWNLOAD_SIZE_MB`; nothing else changes this message or doc row.

**AI assistance:** Claude (Anthropic) helped write this change. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above myself.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Perf][DSv4.1] Mono decode for the DSpark draft layers
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

DSv4.1-Flash mono decode (MI355X, `--monokernel`): the DSpark draft's three layers now run on the mono K1 / K2 kernels too, as ATOM's `DraftMonoRunner` does, instead of vLLM's per-op path. Follow-up to #60397 and #61082; they follow `--monokernel` like the target's layers, with no new switch. Overlaps files with #60731 (gfx942 port), so whichever merges second needs a rebase.

## Claims

- The draft's three layers cost about 227 us of kernel time per step on mono, in place of about 640 us on the original path (graph profile, TP4 c1): about 414 us less GPU time a step.
- AgentX at c1, per-request ITL p50 is 0.030 ms (1.8%) lower than InferenceX's run with `--monokernel`, at TP4 (1.646 against 1.678 ms) and at TP2 (1.970 against 2.000 ms).
- Draft quality is unchanged: DSpark mean acceptance length 3.889 / 3.935 (TP4) and 3.917 (TP2) against 3.899 / 3.896 without, and GSM8K 0.975 / 0.972.
- Target layers' kernels are untouched: their ISA is identical to `main`'s.

## Validation

All on MI355X, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, the InferenceX #3690 recipe, `main` at `ce49c47cbb` plus this PR unless a row says otherwise. "Off" is the same build with the draft layers on vLLM's path (a throwaway env switch for the A/B, not in this PR).

**Layer level.** The draft layers against the original layers on real eager decode steps (TP4 c1 and TP2 c1, 5- and 10-row steps), same inputs: x output cosine >= 0.99975 (relative L2 up to 2.3%, the MoE's top-3 routing near-ties), residual, post / comb / pre mixes >= 0.9999 cosine.

**Acceptance and accuracy** (real block rejection, GSM8K as in InferenceX's DSv4.1-Flash eval: custom `gsm8k` task, chat, 5-shot multiturn, `max_tokens` 12288, 64 requests in flight, full 1,319):

| | draft on mono: GSM8K strict / flexible; mean acceptance length | draft off |
|---|---|---|
| TP4 | 0.9750 / 0.9742; 3.889 (3.935 on the final rebase) | 0.9750 / 0.9742; 3.899 |
| TP2 | 0.9719 / 0.9712; 3.917 | 0.9727 / 0.9719; 3.896 |

**AgentX, c1, 3,600 s** (InferenceX's `infx.bench agentic` client, the #3690 recipe with `--monokernel`, DSpark with synthetic acceptance 3.51, the Rust frontend). Reference: InferenceX's run [38377181342](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/38377181342) (same recipe, nightly 5555a2d8, its own node). TP4 and TP2 ran at the same time on one node. The confidence intervals are bootstrap over the per-request ITL of the profiling phase (about 330 requests an arm).

| | TP4 PR | TP4 ref | TP2 PR | TP2 ref |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ITL p50 (ms), from the summary | 1.650 | 1.680 | 1.970 | 2.000 |
| per-request ITL p50 (ms), diff [95% CI] | 1.646 | 1.678: -0.032 [-0.034, -0.027] | 1.970 | 2.000: -0.030 [-0.034, -0.026] |
| per-request ITL p90 (ms), diff [95% CI] | 1.690 | 1.757: -0.068 [-0.189, +0.012] | 2.053 | 2.178: -0.125 [-0.292, +0.196] |
| interactivity p50 / p90 (tok/s/user) | 607.6 / 591.8 | 596.1 / 569.1 | 507.6 / 487.1 | 499.9 / 459.1 |
| TTFT p50 / p90 (s) | 0.170 / 0.247 | 0.245 / 0.336 | 0.183 / 0.293 | 0.210 / 0.383 |
| E2E p50 (s) | 1.85 | 1.93 | 2.14 | 2.18 |
| requests completed | 335 | 331 | 318 | 316 |

The p50 gain is outside the noise at both TP sizes; the p90 interactivity gain (+4.0% and +6.1%) is not (its interval spans zero), and the TTFT difference is the node, not this PR (prefill is untouched). The reference is not a same-node baseline, so the p50 difference also includes any difference of node, image and commit; an earlier run on the same node of `main` plus only #61934's change (a different kernel change) gave ITL p50 1.670 / 2.000 ms (per-request 1.675 / 1.998).

**Kernel time** (graph-mode torch profile, TP4 c1, draft on mono): K1 about 20 us and K2 about 56 us a layer for the three draft layers (227 us a step); the non-target kernels of a step total 1.76 ms against 2.17 ms with the draft off (excluding all-reduce spin-waits).

**Tests.** `tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_decode.py`: 41 pass, 3 new (the draft layer takes the mono path on its own runner, its first layer takes the broadcast embedding, a layer takes only its own SWA row width). The K1 / K2 ISA of the target builds at TP4, M=6 is identical to `main`'s (`FLYDSL_DUMP_IR` diff: 0 lines).

**Accuracy** (RFC #59665 protocol, as in #60397: thinking on, `reasoning_effort` high, temperature 0.6, top-p 0.95, 8 requests in flight a server, DSpark with block rejection, `--monokernel` so the draft layers run on mono; pass@1, ± is the standard error across questions). The baselines are #60397's numbers; no reference arm of this build was rerun.

| | this PR | #60397 |
|---|---|---|
| TP2 GPQA-Diamond (8 samples a question) | 84.8 ± 2.2 | 85.3 ± 2.2 reference, 85.1 ± 2.2 mono |
| TP2 AIME25 (16 samples a problem) | 98.3 ± 0.9 | 99.4 ± 0.3 reference, 98.3 ± 0.8 mono |
| TP4 GPQA-Diamond (4 samples a question) | 84.5 ± 2.3 | 85.2 ± 2.2 mono |
| TP4 AIME25 (8 samples a problem) | 98.8 ± 0.7 | 100.0 mono (240/240) |

AIME25's wrong samples: 8 of 480 at TP2 (3 empty, out of the 64K budget; 4 on one hard problem) and 3 of 240 at TP4 (1 empty).

**RULER NIAH** (lm-eval, prefix-free chat copies, thinking on, greedy, 40 samples a cell): `niah_single_1`, `niah_multikey_2` and `niah_multikey_3` at 32K, 128K and 256K score 40/40 in every cell at both TP2 and TP4, as in #60397.

## Details

The draft layers are `DeepseekV4DecoderLayer`s with window-only attention (compress ratio 0, no indexer), so the kernels need no new stage. What differs is carried by the build and the step's integers:

- **Routing:** 128 routed experts, top-3 (`dspark_n_routed_experts` / `dspark_num_experts_per_tok`) and one FP4 group per ug task. `MoeBuild` already took these; `MonoBuild` now carries `experts`, `topk`, `ug_groups` and `swa_width` into the MoE stage and the scratch layout.
- **SWA rows:** the draft's metadata is non-causal, with rows `get_dspark_swa_index_width(window, num_speculative_tokens)` wide (192 for window 128 and 5 drafts). K1's key-table stage read the row width as the constant 128; it reads it from the build now.
- **First layer:** the draft hands it the embedding already repeated to the hc copies, `[rows, hc, dim]`; K1 takes it as the settled residual (`fold=False`), as for the target's layer 0.
- **Its own runner:** the scratch layout depends on the number of experts, and a mailbox word must never be a tag to one launch and data to another, so the draft's layers share a second `DSV41MonoLayer` (epoch, scratch, peer buffers) as in ATOM. Every rank creates it at the same layer of the same eager step, like the target's.

Target builds are unchanged: every new field defaults to the target's value, the kernel symbols gain no suffix for them, and the ISA diff above is empty.

Limitations: MI355X (CDNA4), TP2 / TP4, steps of at most 48 rows (the draft's are 5 per request, so up to 8 requests); the layer comparison is on eager steps only. The draft's remaining per-step cost is outside its layers: `_prepare_dflash_inputs` (3 launches of 113 us), the six skinny head GEMMs (279 us), and about 75 small elementwise and copy kernels. I found no open PR doing this. Developed and measured with Claude Code; the submitter's line-by-line review is still pending.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][LoRA] Keep failed activations retryable
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Commit LoRA activation metadata after all layer-loading calls return successfully. A synchronous loading exception currently leaves the adapter marked active, so a retry can skip loading and serve partially copied weights.

## Claims

- Failed activation propagates its exception without marking the adapter active or assigning its GPU slot.
- Retrying a cached adapter executes loading again. An unchanged malformed adapter keeps failing instead of falsely succeeding.
- Successful loading, capacity checks and LRU eviction retain their existing behavior.

## Validation

The CPU regression and real GPU-engine validation below were run on `de8828bf36545fdd414cfd84b1d1480e0c627b7a`. After removing the submitted test and the maintainer's subsequent merge of `main`, the production `vllm/lora/model_manager.py` remains byte-identical at `73be6d45dcc0a15e93edb882ad272d2478f5399a`. The runtime results below predate that merge.

The added regression has been removed from the PR at the maintainer's request. The recorded local regression used the existing manager fixtures and real layer buffers: an incompatible second-layer A tensor made `set_lora` raise; after restoring it, activation had to succeed and copy the restored weights. Both manager implementations were covered. The test file now matches the base exactly.

Before removal of that test, on macOS with the real CPU platform selected explicitly for this source-only installation:

```bash
.venv/bin/python - <<'PY'
import vllm.platforms
from vllm.platforms.cpu import CpuPlatform
vllm.platforms._current_platform = CpuPlatform()
import pytest
raise SystemExit(pytest.main([
    "tests/lora/test_lora_manager.py", "-v", "--tb=short", "-k",
    "failed_lora_activation_can_be_retried or test_lora_model_manager "
    "or test_lora_lru_cache_model_manager or test_lru_lora_model_manager",
]))
PY
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files vllm/lora/model_manager.py tests/lora/test_lora_manager.py
```

The local regression failed on the original source for both managers. On the patch, it and the existing selected lifecycle checks passed. After removing the submitted test, all applicable affected-file pre-commit hooks, including type checking and CI test tethering, passed again.

Real multiprocess GPU-engine validation used NVIDIA L20, TP=1, default Model Runner V2, FP16, eager mode, rank 8, two GPU/CPU adapter slots, prefix caching off, and eight prompts with eight greedy output tokens each. The checkpoint is a deterministic, locally generated OPT model with two layers, hidden size 64 and FFN size 128.

The isolated harness runs the original and patched manager sequentially:

```bash
.venv/bin/python run_engine_validation.py
```

| Engine check | Original | Patched |
| --- | --- | --- |
| One-time exception at the second LoRA layer | Failed adapter remains active; slot assigned | Failed adapter inactive; slot unassigned |
| Same-ID retry compared with a normally loaded reference | 0/8 matching token sequences; maximum selected-logprob difference 0.2615957 | 8/8 matching token sequences; logprob difference 0 |
| Actual malformed checkpoint loaded twice through worker `add_lora` | First call raises; second falsely succeeds | Both calls raise the shape error |
| Replacing the malformed adapter with valid weights | Matches normal reference | Matches normal reference |

Worker extension methods carry primitive RPC arguments and construct `LoRARequest` inside the worker; pickle-based RPC serialization stays disabled. The one-time failure is controlled fault injection, not a hardware-OOM experiment. The malformed-checkpoint check uses an actual tensor-copy shape error.

The engine validation used commit `de8828bf36545fdd414cfd84b1d1480e0c627b7a`, based on `8a8e2baa02cdd3d98ee99dbead0a8c9943a97410`; native components come from the official `be4ce2e50545c6c1bf13f224022aeb2bcf0c0070` nightly wheel. Compiled sources and the affected LoRA files are unchanged between that wheel commit and the base. GPU runtime: Torch 2.14.1+cu130, Transformers 5.19.0 and Triton 3.8.0. Multi-GPU serving was not tested. These checks establish loading/retry correctness; no accuracy or throughput improvement is claimed.

## Details

Only the two metadata writes move. The submitted test was removed in `6e8d27da` following review; the effective PR diff now contains only this production file. The existing copy/reset loop and return contract are unchanged, with no additional allocation or synchronization. Physical buffers may still contain partial data after an exception, but no adapter ID is assigned to that slot; the next activation executes the existing loading/reset loop.

Open-PR searches and relevant diffs were checked. #60039 validates module-name matching, #60222 compensates failed loads in the Rust frontend, and #59819 exposes slot read/update operations. They do not defer the worker manager's activation commit after a synchronous layer-loading exception. Related overlap-loading and cache-observability PRs were also checked.

AI assistance was used: Codex prepared the implementation and validation. The submitting human confirmed reviewing every changed line and personally running the relevant validation before publication.

commits.pr_title: [Model] Add Reflection Beam
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Add day-0 support for Reflection's Beam-1.0 (`BeamForCausalLM`), a 501B-parameter MoE with 23B active parameters, and its DFlash2 drafter (`DFlash2BeamDraftModel`). This is the model slice of #61978.

Builds on #62042 (merged). This PR doesn't need FlashInfer nightly. The `beam` reasoning and tool parsers are in #62052. The fused MNNVL all-reduce (with Beam's norm and MoE-finalize epilogue) is split out into a stacked follow-up PR. MegaMoE support (attention DP + expert parallelism on FlashInfer CuTeDSL), which does need FlashInfer nightly, follows in #62073.

## Claims

- **Architecture:**
  - hybrid sliding-window (RoPE) and full-attention NoPE layers with SSMax;
  - per-head Q/K norm and a sigmoid output gate;
  - DeepSeek-V3-style MoE with an FP32 router;
  - sandwich norms and depth-scaled residuals.

  It runs with tensor, data or expert parallelism. `BeamConfig` and the model follow the released `config.json` schema (`layer_types`, `mlp_layer_types`, per-type `rope_parameters`); behavior the release does not configure is fixed rather than switchable.
- **Fused kernels for Blackwell**, under `vllm/models/beam/nvidia`: attention, norm/residual boundaries, and DFlash2 context ops. TP all-reduce uses vLLM's standard path in this PR.
- **DFlash2 speculative decoding:** works with FP8 KV cache and adaptive verification. The Beam drafter is self-contained and does not subclass the Qwen3 DFlash classes.

## Validation

**Serving:** Beam-1.0 NVFP4 + DFlash2 (7 draft tokens), TP8 on GB200, SPEED-Bench `throughput_1k` low-entropy subset, greedy decoding. *Measured on the previous revision, which included the fused all-reduce; re-run on this revision pending.*

The released `config.json` files for `reflection/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B` and `-NVFP4` also load through `get_config` (9 NoPE layers, 3 dense layers).

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Bugfix] Release vLLM's communicators on external-launcher shutdown
commits.pr_body:
Motivation: https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/95633/list?jid=01a14c8b-4acc-4866-b9b8-e31d71cdc245&tab=output

`ExecutorWithExternalLauncher` (torchrun, `distributed_executor_backend="external_launcher"`) now destroys vLLM's model-parallel groups on shutdown, like `MultiprocExecutor`'s workers do. Without it, `:amd: (MI355) Distributed DP + EP` intermittently aborts at exit on the ROCm 10 image (#58761).

- Fixes the exit-time abort (`terminate called without an active exception`, SIGABRT on several ranks) of `examples/features/torchrun/torchrun_dp_example_offline.py --tp-size=2 --dp-size=4 --enable-ep` on MI355 with ROCm 10.
- Only vLLM-owned groups are destroyed; the world group and the default process group, which the launcher may own, are untouched.

Root cause: `UniProcExecutor.shutdown()` only calls `worker.shutdown()`. `MultiprocExecutor` additionally calls `destroy_model_parallel()` and `destroy_distributed_environment()`, which abort the PyNCCL communicators and destroy the NCCL subgroups. In external-launcher mode nothing does, so each rank exits with live RCCL communicators whose background threads are destroyed by static destructors; a `std::thread` destroyed while joinable calls `std::terminate`. ROCm 7.2's RCCL tolerates this; ROCm 10's does not, intermittently.

---

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Attention] Fix Triton MLA decode int32 overflow and logits workspace accounting
commits.pr_body:
Triton MLA models crash at their default context length on MI355: `vllm serve` with default settings for Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct, LongCat-Flash-Lite-FP8 and DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat dies with `Memory access fault by GPU ... Write access to a read-only page` during CUDA graph capture. Two bugs are involved, and the second only shows up once the first is fixed:

1. **int32 overflow in the decode kernels.** The split-KV logits offset `cur_batch * stride_mid_ob` is computed in int32. At ≥ 128K context, `_compute_num_kv_splits` picks 512 splits on MI355 (2 × 256 CUs), so with 32 heads one request's logits span 32 × 512 × 513 = 8.4M floats. From batch row 256 onward the offset passes 2^31, and FULL graph capture runs batches up to 512.
2. **The logits workspace is not counted by memory profiling.** #46819 reserves the worst-case logits workspace (32 GiB for LongCat at defaults: 1024 seqs × 32 heads × 512 splits × 513 × fp32) when the metadata builder is created, which happens after profiling. The KV cache is then sized as if that memory were free, and its allocation OOMs (`Tried to allocate 164.67 GiB`, 157.84 GiB free).

To resolve the above, this PR modifies:
- `triton_decode_attention.py`: compute `cur_batch * stride_mid_ob` in int64 at the six logits offsets (stage 1 normal/grouped stores and stage 2 loads), following #47671.
- `MLAAttentionImpl.reserve_profiling_workspace()`: a no-op hook called from the MLA profiling branch, next to the existing `kv_b_proj` scratch simulation.
- `TritonMLAImpl` overrides the hook to reserve the logits workspace at its upper bound (`max_num_seqs × max_decode_query_len`) during profiling. The builder keeps its reservation, which becomes a no-op.
- `test_triton_decode_attention.py`: a regression test whose logits exceed 2^31 elements, for the grouped (MLA) and normal kernels.

## Validation

MI355, TP1. `main` vs this PR:

| | `main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct, default 1M context | memory access fault | serves, GSM8K 87.34 |
| LongCat-Flash-Lite-FP8, default 320K context | memory access fault | serves, GSM8K 86.88 |
| DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat, default backend (`TRITON_MLA`) and 160K context | memory access fault | serves |
| LongCat with only the overflow fix | — | OOM at KV cache allocation |
| LongCat with only the accounting fix | — | memory access fault |

Both models were also served at concurrency 384, where decode rows ≥ 256 run with 512 splits: 0 failed requests.

At 32K context, where `main` works (decode TPOT Δ, + is faster; median of 5 reps, repeated with GPUs swapped):

| Model | C1 | C8 | C32 | C128 | GSM8K main → PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct | +0.4 / +0.3% | +0.2 / +0.3% | −0.1 / +2.1% | +2.2 / +2.1% | 86.88 → 86.58 (McNemar p = 0.75) |
| LongCat-Flash-Lite-FP8 | +1.0 / +0.6% | +1.7 / +1.6% | +3.6 / +3.0% | +6.0 / +5.3% | 86.88 → 87.34 (p = 0.57) |

<details>
<summary>Why decode got faster</summary>

A rocprofv3 trace of the same LongCat decode workload (128 × 2048-token prompts, 256 output tokens, 32K context) shows all of the difference in `_fwd_grouped_kernel_stage1`: 6062 → 5230 ms (−13.7%), with identical grids and register counts. Every other kernel is within ±0.5%. In the stage-1 variants I inspected, the int32 offset lowers the logits stores to scalar `buffer_store_dword`, while the int64 base produces vectorized `global_store_dwordx3`. The kernel microbenchmark is neutral at long sequences (30 shapes, H 16–128, 4K–128K context: median 1.000×, range 0.990–1.005×, run-to-run drift ≤ 0.8%) and 15–17% faster at 512 splits with batch ≥ 128.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Tests</summary>

- `test_decode_attention_int64_logits_offset` faults on `main` (both cases) and passes with this PR in 2.4 s. It uses ~8.6 GB of fp32 logits.
- `tests/kernels/attention/test_triton_decode_attention.py` + `test_triton_mla_causal_verify_flatten.py`: 133 passed, 10/10 loops.
- `v1/attention/test_mla_backends.py` + `test_sparse_mla_backends.py` (the CI command): 11 clean runs (751 passed), including all 6 with `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1`. The 7 other runs failed only in tests that behave the same on `main`:
  - The sparse `ROCMAiterMLA` decode test fails about 1 in 20 in isolation: 19/20 on both `main` and this PR.
  - HF API 429 rate limits, from four loops running in parallel.
  - `test_chunked_context_backend_correctness` failed only in runs that also hit 429s. It is 20/20 in isolation on both `main` and this PR.
  - One transient engine OOM, where device-wide free memory dropped during profiling.
- `v1/attention` (rest of the CI command, CI environment): 1972 passed.
- DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat on `ROCM_AITER_MLA` (`VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=0`), where the hook is a no-op, serves normally. AITER MoE was turned off only because this image's AITER `topk_gating` rejects `num_shared_experts` on `main`.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Design notes</summary>

- **Effect on KV cache size:** the KV cache now excludes the logits workspace. LongCat at 32K goes from 164.67 to 162.91 GiB (`main` over-commits there too, but its slack absorbs it). At 320K it is 134.86 GiB, where `main` cannot start.
- **Upper bound:** the profiling hook has no builder, so it sizes rows as `max_num_seqs × max_decode_query_len`. That matches the builder's `reorder_batch_threshold` except with DCP on a backend without varlen support, where the builder uses 1 and the profiled reservation is larger than needed.
- **Why the profiling forward:** the impl is built at model load, but the decode metadata builder only exists after profiling. Reserving in the profiling run follows the existing MLA `kv_b_proj` simulation and the sparse-indexer reservations, and avoids touching the worker's profiling code.
- **History:** #33529 made split counts up to 2 × compute units reachable, and #46819 moved the logits into a workspace reserved after profiling. #47671 fixed the same overflow class for page offsets in these kernels.
- **Duplicate check:** no open PR or issue covers this. #46728 (NVIDIA shared-memory OOR) and #57094 (NaN on empty `seq_len`) touch the same kernels for different bugs.

</details>

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][CI] Contain the MI355 DP + EP exit-time abort
commits.pr_body:
- Drop `optional: false` from the MI355 DP + EP mirror so it inherits the parent's `optional: true` and stops gating PR builds
- Export `NCCL_RAS_ENABLE=0` in the mirror's commands, with a TODO to drop it once ROCm/rocm-systems#13572 is fixed
- Export `TORCH_CPP_LOG_LEVEL=INFO` so ProcessGroupNCCL teardown is logged per process group

Since the ROCm 10 image became the default (#58761), the torchrun DP + EP example finishes generating on all eight ranks, and about 15 s later one to five ranks abort on the main thread with `terminate called without an active exception` (https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/95651, https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/95663). The root cause is still under investigation; it does not reproduce with two ranks, and vLLM already defaults `NCCL_RAS_ENABLE=0` on ROCm, so the export here only pins it for this step rather than fixing the abort. The commands are listed on the mirror because `env:` does not reach the AMD test container, and the teardown logs (about 60 lines per rank) should show which process group, if any, stalls before the abort.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to draft this change. Every line was reviewed by the submitter.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][CI] Pin Inductor pointwise configs in the MoRIIO dummy-weight P/D test
commits.pr_body:
- Turn off Inductor pointwise autotuning (`triton.autotune_pointwise`) next to deterministic mode in `test_write_dummy_e2e_rocm.py`, and update the comment and docstring that explain why

Since the ROCm 10 image became the default (#58761), the attention-only cases fail with first-token log-prob distances of one or two bf16 steps (0.03-0.14), e.g. https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/95663. P/D is not involved: two plain direct serves of the same model on the same GPU disagree by the same amount, while each server is bitwise stable across repeats. Inductor's deterministic mode only pins reduction configs and still picks the XBLOCK of pointwise kernels by timing. On ROCm the XBLOCK changes which multiply-adds of the fused QK-norm + RoPE kernel get contracted into FMAs (e.g. 4 unfused packed adds at XBLOCK 1024, none at 4096), and the candidates are within timing noise of each other, so each server ends up with a random config. Pinning every pointwise kernel's config in two fresh processes makes them agree bitwise; flipping only the QK-norm + RoPE kernel's XBLOCK reproduces the CI distances.

With this change the CI-failing `qwen3_dense-TRITON_ATTN-P_FULL_AND_PIECEWISE-D_FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` case passes 10/10 on MI355 with ROCm 10 (distances exactly 0.0, full external prefix-cache hits).

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][KV Connector] Pair non-divisible hybrid MLA block sizes in NixlConnector
commits.pr_body:
NixlConnector now pairs P/D blocks of a hybrid MLA model when neither block size divides the other. That happens when P and D run different TP on ROCm. Kimi-K3 with P TP2 (2944-token blocks) and D TP1 (5760) used to fail the handshake and now runs.  Hybrid block sizes follow the TP-sharded SSM page, so P and D pick different sizes when their TP differs. On CUDA, MLA backends force 64-token kernel blocks, so the sizes always divide. ROCm AITER MLA accepts any kernel block size, so `block_size_ratio` asserts. During the handshake, `_split_remote_blocks` now views the remote blocks as gcd-sized kernel blocks (2944 → 23 × 128). The existing `block_size_ratio > 1` path then pairs them with D's 45 sub-blocks and zeroes the untransferred tail. This only applies to hybrid MLA with plainly strided remote regions. With prefix caching on, D still rejects such pairs through the existing hybrid check, as on CUDA.

- Hybrid MLA P/D with non-divisible block sizes transfers in gcd-sized units (128 tokens for Kimi-K3) instead of asserting at the handshake.
- Pairs that work today never reach the new code, so they are unaffected.

On MI355 with AITER MLA:
- `test_prefix_cache.py -k pd-tp2-dep2` (Kimi-K3): failed the handshake before; now 4/4 pass, 10/10 runs.
- Also added a new `test_hetero_non_divisible_block_sizes`: 28 fail before, 28 pass after.

The model-level runs used `moonshotai/Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct` with NIXL P/D, 5 interleaved runs per column, each with fresh servers. Values are mean ± sd.

| `vllm bench serve` (4096 in / 128 out, conc 16) | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| P TP2 → D TP1, equal 2048 blocks: req/s | 3.478 ± 0.077 | 3.480 ± 0.045 |
| P TP2 → D TP1, equal 2048 blocks: TPOT (ms) | 29.54 ± 0.65 | 29.36 ± 0.55 |
| P TP2 → D TP1, 1024 → 1920: req/s | handshake assert | 3.432 ± 0.027 |

| gsm8k strict-match (5-shot, n=1319) | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| P TP2 → D TP1, equal 2048 blocks | 0.8748 ± 0.0034 | 0.8748 ± 0.0025 |
| P TP2 → D TP1, 1024 → 1920 | handshake assert | 0.8748 ± 0.0020 |
| P TP1 → D TP2, 1920 → 1024 | handshake assert | 0.8732 ± 0.0031 |

The existing ROCm NIXL P/D accuracy groups also pass.
